body:
This is what it comes down to: The sitting President of the United States is trying to exert direct control over the U.S. Postal Service to get around the Constitution, which says that states have control of elections. Courts are stopping him from directly suppressing mail-in ballots, so he's trying an end run around them using USPS.
Trump and the MAGA movement want to pick and choose whose vote counts. RUSH $35 or whatever you can right now to fight back against this abuse of the USPS and our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050426_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Signs Order Seeking Federal Control of Mail Voting as He Promotes False Claims [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050426_3&amount=25]
Straight from the New York Times , Team:
" President Trump on [March 31] stepped up efforts to promote his false claims of widespread voting fraud, signing an executive order of questionable constitutionality seeking to create a national list of citizens that would determine voting eligibility and restrict mail ballots. "
Let's be clear: The president has no explicit Constitutional authority over elections, and much of this latest attack on our fundamental right to vote appears difficult to enforce and legally dubious.
This order directs the Department of Homeland Security to create a “ state citizenship list ” based on data from various federal databases. It also directs federal officials to send that made-up list to state election officials, and orders the attorney general to prioritize prosecution of election officials who provide ballots to voters not on the made-up list. It also directs the U.S. Postal Service not to transmit mail-in ballots from any individual not included on Trump's “ state citizenship list ," even though elections are mandated by the constitutional the be run by the states.
This order is yet another sign that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
Our elections are sound and mail-in voting is secure, no matter what Trump says. Step up to defend our fundamental right to vote and the use of mail-in ballots with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050426_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=050426_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=050426_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?express_lane=true&refcode=050426_3&amount=50]

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . States have spent millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing. It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
But that doesn't stop Trump because he's absolutely terrified of what might happen in the next election.
Arizona’s Secretary of State (the official who runs elections), Adrian Fontes, reacted like this: “ The Constitution doesn’t allow the executive to take over elections administration, that’s a job for the state legislatures or Congress, and so I don’t think this is going to pass any sort of judicial muster. So this is a big, giant waste of time, and it’s an attention grab from the Trump administration. ”
He added: “ The greatest threat to American elections is Donald Trump lying about them. ” That''s because Donald Trump’s continued claims about large-scale “cheating” in elections are outright lies.
Protecting vote-by-mail for the upcoming midterms is crucial to make every voice heard in our elections. Will you chip in $35 or whatever you can to fight lies about mail-in voting and help make every vote count? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050426_3&amount=35]

These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Patriot - The “No Kings” crowd just stood up and applauded a King.

You can’t make this up.

A foreign monarch walked into the United States Congress, referred to himself as “the sovereign,” and our elected officials grinned, clapped, and gave him the royal treatment.

That’s not public service. That’s submission.

**And the worst part? It wasn’t just one party. It was the whole UniParty machine on display.**

RINOs. Chuck Schumer. Amy Klobuchar. Republicans and Democrats standing together, applauding power, corruption, and foreign influence while pretending they work for you.

Let me be clear:

**There is only one King — Jesus Christ.**

America has no sovereign but the people.

No crown. No commonwealth. No ruling class.

**This is the United States of America, and our elected officials should be defending American citizens, not bowing before foreign elites.**

That’s why I’m running.

Because Washington is rotten. Because the UniParty is real. Because Minnesota deserves a fighter who will not bend the knee.

I’m not going to Congress to clap for kings.

**I’m going to fight for the American people.**

And the truth is still undefeated.

name: Wes Moore
subject: Leave no one behind
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| It’s Governor Wes Moore.

Five years ago, I had never run for political office. I was a former Army Captain, a dad to two young kids, and I ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country.

But I knew more had to be done. While career politicians were saying that everything was great, **I was hearing from folks all across Maryland who were feeling left behind.** So I ran for Governor with a mission to make Maryland a state that serves all our people — and won. (And I’m not done yet!)

**Our mission must continue this year.** I’m running for re-election so we can keep building on the progress we’ve made on jobs, education, public safety, and more. There are tough fights on the horizon, and there’s so much more for us to accomplish together.

[I’m asking you to join our team by chipping in $5 or $10 right now, split between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project. Every dollar we raise helps defend this seat and build a campaign that’s ready for the challenges ahead.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108747?t=6&akid=24197%2E878179%2EyXJZoa) If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Wes Moore and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108748?t=7&akid=24197%2E878179%2EyXJZoa)

We’re making real progress — investing historic amounts in public education, bringing down costs for working families, and making our communities safer.

But we’re still in the federal government’s line of sight. Donald Trump has attacked me before, and he and his powerful GOP allies are going to do everything possible to flip our state back to red come November. This election could be an uphill battle.

**This powerful team has never backed down from a fight and I know you are not about to start now.** We have to hit the ground running, because our momentum now determines how we’re able to run the rest of this campaign.

[Please, split a $10 donation between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project today. Every donation helps us start the next phase of our campaign strong and fight back against Republicans’ advantage.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/108747?t=12&akid=24197%2E878179%2EyXJZoa)

It’s time for us to come together again, across places and party lines, to prove to a dysfunctional Washington that there’s a better way forward.

Elevate,

Wes

name: Rep. Gloria Johnson
subject: Stand up against the shameful GOP power grab
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF GLORIA JOHNSON, LISA SORENSEN, TREASURER
body:
We need to call this special session what it is: a white power rally.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/ec05bffd610c/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab?e=dc5f639d62)
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| |
Friends,
You’ve probably seen the news: Governor Bill Lee is rushing state legislators to a special session on Tuesday (tomorrow), at the direction of his boss Donald Trump, in order to redraw our state’s political districts. They’re trying to steal Tennessee’s only Democratic-held Congressional seat, and ensure that Republicans don’t ever have to compete with Democrats at all for federal representation.
**We need to call this special session what it is: a white power rally.** By breaking up Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District, Republicans are silencing the voices of Black voters, who make up a majority of Shelby County and 60% of the district. Generations of brave Americans - including countless Tennesseans - fought for equal rights and representation and fought against Jim Crow-era codified racism. Now, Bill Lee and Marsha Blackburn want to undo that progress and drag us back to the darkest corners of our history.
[**TAKE ACTION HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/x4N2LLr1N8T?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
**This is a shameful power grab** , and I’m sickened by our governor and the bootlicking Republican supermajority. Perhaps they should review our own Tennessee law (TN Code § 2-16-102) that says “The districts may not be changed between apportionments.”
They don’t care that Tennessee is [ranked dead last for K-12 education spending](https://us.list-manage.com/13CXkQkuINC?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) or that farms are going bankrupt, rural hospitals are at risk of closing, and prices are skyrocketing... they only care about clinging to power and appeasing their DC bosses.
**But we are not powerless in this moment**. We need to stand tall, stand together, and STOP these extremists before the damage is done. You can show up and speak out in the coming days to let Bill Lee and Marsha Blackburn know that **Tennessee is a lot more than just MAGA bootlickers** , and we deserve representation too. You can add your name to this petition today to say “Tennessee Is Home”:
[**SIGN THE PETITION**](https://us.list-manage.com/lcbo_xoiQZF?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
And finally, I will not be able to take donations once the special session starts so if you can, please donate tonight to help us fight back against this power grab.
[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/t4_dt2zjeyP?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
I’ll be in touch with you again this week, so please stay tuned and be prepared to take any action you can to stop this reckless power grab.
In solidarity,Gloria JohnsonState RepresentativeTennessee House District 90

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: 3 Weeks Out - Republicans Undecided
body:
Plus: Iran's regime is cracking | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1CxBH3N40LX?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Three weeks until New Mexicans pick a Republican nominee for governor. The new [Albuquerque Journal poll just dropped](https://us.list-manage.com/ST7GHSdsscv?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) — and it tells you everything about how wide open this thing still is.

Then we get to Iran. The regime is cracking. And what the Wall Street Journal just reported that they're considering...well, you have to hear it to believe it!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/_Xst7P0AJqE?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🏛️ **HULL LEADS AT 30% — 40% STILL HAVEN'T DECIDED**
Gregg Hull is in front. Doug Turner is at 21%. Duke Rodriguez is stuck in single digits.
But the number that actually matters is 40% — that's how many Republican and Independent voters still haven't picked a candidate. Three weeks out.
We break down why nobody has been able to lay a glove on Hull, and the one move Doug Turner has to make in the next 14 days — or this race is over.

🔥 **THE ATTACK MAILERS HIT — AND ONE OF THEM ACTUALLY LANDS**
Duke Rodriguez voted in Arizona in 2024. And 2022. And 2018. And 2016.
A PAC mailer just made sure every Republican primary voter knows it.
Meanwhile, Duke's people are firing back at Doug Turner over $6 million in state contracts Turner's firm allegedly took from Michelle Lujan Grisham to push her COVID agenda.
We watch both candidates' ads on the show. One is professional. The other looks — well, you'll see. And we tell you which attack insiders say is actually working.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/7K00f9F4Wmn?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🐬 **IRAN'S REGIME IS CRACKING — AND THEY'RE PLOTTING KAMIKAZE DOLPHINS**
70% inflation. Hundreds of millions in losses every day. No oil moving to China. The Iranian regime is desperate.
How desperate? The Wall Street Journal just reported they're contemplating strapping mines to dolphins to go after U.S. ships.
That's not a joke. That's actually being floated.
Mark walks through why Trump's blockade is working better than the media wants to admit — and why Scott Jennings completely lost his cool on CNN this week. We're not defending Jennings. But you have to see what triggered it.

✈️ **WARREN AND BUTTIGIEG JUST TOOK DOWN SPIRIT AIRLINES**
Spirit went bankrupt Saturday. 30 regional airports lost service overnight.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent named names on Sunday morning TV: Elizabeth Warren wrote the letter that blocked the JetBlue merger. Pete Buttigieg's DOT killed the deal.
Why does it matter to you in Albuquerque? Half the Sunport's traffic flies Southwest. And when Spirit's discount flyers disappear from connecting hubs, your fares are about to go up across the board. Mark explains exactly how this hits your wallet.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/ufgcHdCWoRU?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

PLUS: A Hollywood reality star is running for LA Mayor against Karen Bass — and his ad, filmed standing in an Airstream parked on his burned-out home, is one of the most effective candidate spots we've seen all year. We also break down the new study showing millennial dads have **tripled** the time they spend with their kids since the 1960s.

Peter – the President Trump-stacked Supreme Court just gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which bans racially discriminatory electoral laws and maps.
**_[If that’s all you need to hear, please take 60 seconds right now to sign on to Roy’s emergency petition in support of fair representation and voting rights before 11:59 p.m.](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk416&t=9&akid=1288%2E124072%2EAJKcWI)_**

---
**By effectively empowering GOP-held state legislatures to silence millions of voters of color – _and millions of North Carolinians_ – ahead of the midterms, the _Louisiana v. Callais_ ruling is an egregious attack on the better part of a century’s worth of progress. It also risks giving MAGA Republicans all the seats they need to lock in control of the House for decades to come.**
The Supreme Court has joined President Trump and his congressional allies in chipping away at the very idea that in our democracy, every vote matters equally.

However, this appalling decision only underscores what Roy has said before: **Democracy is not something guaranteed to us – it’s something we must fight for. **
**_[That’s why we’re counting on at least 50,000 folks like you to join the fight alongside him in support of fair representation and voting rights ASAP. Will you please take 60 seconds now to add your name to our emergency petition before the deadline at midnight?](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk416&t=11&akid=1288%2E124072%2EAJKcWI)_**

They don't want the stronger candidate, they want one who will bend to corporate donors. | | | Peter, Just like they did in Maine, the Democratic establishment is trying to put their thumb on the scale in another primary — not to support the stronger candidate, but the candidate who will bend to their corporate donors. **The DCCC just announced they are going to try to derail WFP champion Randy Villegas in his race for Congress in California’s 22nd Congressional district.** Because they know he’s not the type of candidate to blindly push their preferred agenda — instead, he’ll fight for working families day in and day out. And corporate donors can’t allow that. Randy has all the momentum in this race right now, and the Democratic establishment is panicking. He is the top Democratic fundraiser in the race, despite not taking a penny from corporate interests. The son of Mexican immigrants, **he would also be the first Latino representative that CA-22 — which is 73% Latino — has ever had.** In a district on the front lines of defending immigrant neighbors from ICE, the establishment is backing Jasmeet Bains, who refused to vote on a bill that requires ICE agents to lower their masks. clean_body: They don't want the stronger candidate, they want one who will bend to corporate donors. | | | Peter, Just like they did in Maine, the Democratic establishment is trying to put their thumb on the scale in another primary — not to support the stronger candidate, but the candidate who will bend to their corporate donors. The DCCC just announced they are going to try to derail WFP champion Randy Villegas in his race for Congress in California’s 22nd Congressional district. Because they know he’s not the type of candidate to blindly push their preferred agenda — instead, he’ll fight for working families day in and day out. And corporate donors can’t allow that. Randy has all the momentum in this race right now, and the Democratic establishment is panicking. He is the top Democratic fundraiser in the race, despite not taking a penny from corporate interests. The son of Mexican immigrants, he would also be the first Latino representative that CA-22 — which is 73% Latino — has ever had. In a district on the front lines of defending immigrant neighbors from ICE, the establishment is backing Jasmeet Bains, who refused to vote on a bill that requires ICE agents to lower their masks. This will be one of the most competitive races of 2026, and Randy is the obvious choice for working families in California. He’s racked up more key endorsements than his opponent, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, Dolores Huerta, the Congressional Progressive Caucus, the National Education Association, the United Autoworkers, and National Nurses United. Meanwhile, Jasmeet Bains has raked in money from corporate donors — many of whom have donated to the district’s Republican incumbent in the past. Bains was also the only Democrat in the Assembly to vote against Prop 50, Newsom's Election Rigging Response Act. Randy Villegas is the ONLY candidate in this race with the energy and momentum to defeat incumbent Republican David Valadao in November. But first, we need to overcome these attacks by the corporate Democratic establishment. In solidarity, Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Reply directly to this email and let us know. This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If you received this email as a forward and want to get the latest updates from the Working Families Party directly, The Working Families Party is the party of the multiracial working class, fighting for a nation that cares for all of us. **TOP NEWS**
**" Exclusive: Texas teacher accused of molesting student was on 'do not hire' list"** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/628f21b5-b9d4-4257-9c2a-5b5b766e484e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)' **Bayliss Wagner** - Youths walk by the windows of the dining hall on their way to lunch in 2006 at the Giddings State School in Giddings, Texas. When one of their teachers was arrested and accused of repeatedly molesting an eighth-grade student last fall, Elgin school district officials expressed shock.

"Accusations such as these are concerning, and if proven to be true, unacceptable," the Austin-area district told KVUE in November, noting they had moved quickly to assist police when the claims were made against **Turran Fennix**.

But it wasn't the first time that Fennix, 34, had been accused of having inappropriate interactions with a child, according to records obtained by Hearst Newspapers. Two years earlier, Texas' juvenile justice agency barred Fennix from future work in the system after he was caught giving a skin-to-skin back massage to a student in a dorm room, a clear policy violation. Administrators determined he should be fired for the incident, but allowed him to resign instead. Elgin Middle School hired him just a few months later.

Fennix's previously unreported trajectory from the Texas Juvenile Justice Department to a middle school raises questions about how thoroughly Elgin vetted the employee and whether the state disclosed his full background. _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/628f21b5-b9d4-4257-9c2a-5b5b766e484e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" As the state targets cities over ICE policies, Austin considers next steps"** via [TPR](https://substack.com/redirect/b9e1f541-f5c5-4a8d-8a81-3d9547697b27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Mose Buchele** - In some ways, Texas has provided a crystal ball for the rest of the country when it comes to immigration policy. Before the Trump administration poured billions into immigration enforcement and built partnerships between local police and state and federal immigration agents, Texas was already doing it. So, for those opposed to the deportation surge, Texas is worth paying attention to.

That was one of the takeaways from a panel Saturday at the KUT Festival. "**Kristin Etter** , the director of policy and legal services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, said, "Here in Texas, we have kind of a four- to five-year head start when it comes to the rest of the country. We have operated a program called Operation Lone Star that has used state resources. So we have a model here in Texas for this police/ICE collaboration."

Another takeaway from the panel: In a state where much of the voting public and all state political leaders support aggressive immigration enforcement, opposition becomes local. In liberal Austin, local leaders have tried to craft policies that would limit police partnering with ICE, but the governor took notice and the Austin Police Department had to soften one policy under threat of funding cuts.

City Council Member **Zo Qadri** said Austin still has tools at its disposal "to make sure that folks are protected and are safe." City Council Member **Jos e Velasquez** pointed to millions in city funding for local immigration advocacy groups and the council's support for Austin's "safe to call" initiative as examples. _([TPR](https://substack.com/redirect/b9e1f541-f5c5-4a8d-8a81-3d9547697b27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Tornado in North Texas Destroys Several Buildings and Displaces Residents"** via [The New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/1ba47b22-3ceb-4d59-a70b-898010932a6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Jesus Jim enez **- The whir of chain saws and the beeping of utility trucks were the most prominent sounds around Mineral Wells, Texas, on Wednesday afternoon, after a tornado the previous night ripped through a section of the city.

In one industrial sector of Mineral Wells, a town of about 15,000 residents west of the Dallas-Fort Worth area, roofs had been sheared off buildings and other structures had been reduced to piles of what looked like matchsticks. But the destruction appeared limited to an area of commercial properties that were largely empty.

Most residential homes in the area were unscathed, and no deaths were reported, though at least five people were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries and many residents were displaced, city officials said.

**Christopher Hester** , 33, said that he was sitting in his living room with his wife on Tuesday afternoon when their front door suddenly burst open. He said they immediately took cover in the hallway of their home. _([The New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/1ba47b22-3ceb-4d59-a70b-898010932a6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" High gas prices eating into Texans' budgets, fueling inflation"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/2530c8ae-cb49-499f-9038-da088809b741?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Paul Cobler** and**Colleen DeGuzman** - The large signs outside of gas stations across Texas intended to catch drivers' eyes are lately doing so for all the wrong reasons.

At a Valero gas station in Edinburg, **Reynaldo Zarazoa** , who installs tile for a living and has to haul tools and equipment around in his gray GMC pickup, watched Thursday as the display on the gas pump reached $78 -- nearly a fifth of his weekly income.

"My work is cheap and the gas is expensive," said Zarazoa, a father of two living in Peñitas, a small city in the Rio Grande Valley. "But I have to drive every day, every day for work."

The price of fuel has risen significantly since the U.S.-Israel war on Iran began on Feb. 28, closing a key international shipping lane for oil and gas, the Strait of Hormuz. The average price for a gallon of gas in Texas was $2.55 in early February, according to AAA. It had risen to $3.78 on Wednesday morning. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/2530c8ae-cb49-499f-9038-da088809b741?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Court sides with 'EPIC City' developers over state agency in fair housing fight"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/07443e71-f930-448a-9d7d-de7dd85d2189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Nick Wooten** - "This ruling confirms what we have maintained from the beginning -- that Community Capital Partners has been willing, ready, and committed to following Texas law at every step," said Imran Chaudhary pictured above at the EPIC City project site outside of Josephine.

A Travis County judge has ordered a state agency to comply with the fair housing agreement it made with the developer of a Muslim-centric neighborhood in North Texas.

The Texas Workforce Commission must abide by the terms of a September 2025 settlement it reached with developer Community Capital Partners. The group is behind The Meadow, previously called EPIC City.

The 201st District Court issued the injunction Tuesday. A judge also denied the state's request to dismiss the case on Wednesday, allowing Community Capital Partners' lawsuit to move forward. _([DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/07443e71-f930-448a-9d7d-de7dd85d2189?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
* * *
**2026**
**" Republican Brett Ligon, former Montgomery County DA, wins special election for Texas Senate seat"** via Texas Tribune's**Alejandro Serrano** and **Colleen DeGuzman** -**Brett Ligon,** the Republican former district attorney of Montgomery County, won a special election Saturday for the state Senate district vacated by **Brandon Creighton** , who was tapped last year to be chancellor of the Texas Tech University System.

Ligon defeated Democrat **Ron Angeletti** , an educator and small-business owner who was the only other candidate on the ballot. The two are set for a rematch in November for a full four-year term. In the meantime, Ligon will serve the remainder of Creighton's term, which runs until the start of the next legislative session in January.

"The voters of SD4 have delivered a clear message tonight. Conservative values and Republican dominance in Texas are alive and well," he said in a statement declaring victory 25 minutes after polls closed. "Democrats from Texas and all over the country threw everything they had at us. Democrat politicians were here today in full force, campaigning hard for my opponent. As if we had been flying the 'Come and Take It' flag - they tried - and they failed."

Senate District 4 - which spans across Chambers, Harris, Jefferson, and Montgomery counties - voted for President **Donald Trump** by a 34-point margin in 2024, making it one of the reddest seats in the upper chamber. It is considered a virtual lock for Republicans in November, even with midterm political headwinds that have left Democrats optimistic about flipping GOP legislative seats. _([Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/b9efb17d-e6c1-4ad7-9766-faaf08ceb3be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" 'It's a mess': With no Trump endorsement in Texas Senate race, Cornyn and Paxton are locked in an expensive brawl"** via [CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/b3854ffd-8a6a-4d70-969c-a58d981fad89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Patrick Svitek** - Nearly two months ago, President **Donald Trump** promised he would make an endorsement "soon" in the Republican primary runoff for US Senate in Texas. That endorsement still has not arrived -- and its absence is keeping the race highly competitive.

Three people involved in the race said they no longer expected Trump to get involved in the battle between Sen. **John Cornyn** and Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton**. However, they cautioned he could change his mind before the May 26 runoff, keeping both sides on edge in the final weeks.

While Democrats haven't won statewide in Texas since 1994, they have a Senate nominee in state Rep. **James Talarico** who is energizing liberals ahead of the November midterms and raising massive sums. Republicans long wanted to avoid a damaging runoff that could make things easier for Talarico, in part by having Trump boost one candidate and pressure the other to back down.

Trump was likely to eventually endorse Cornyn after he and Paxton advanced from a March 3 primary, sources told CNN at the time. However, Trump grew frustrated after Republican operatives leaked his expected plans, the sources said. Trump also fielded calls from some of his most ardent supporters, pushing him not to endorse Cornyn and warning it would be a mistake with his "Make America Great Again" base. _([CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/b3854ffd-8a6a-4d70-969c-a58d981fad89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

Talarico led U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** 40% to 33% in a potential matchup, and held a 42% to 34% advantage over Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , the University of Texas at Austin's Texas Politics Project survey found. In both cases, 19% of voters said they were still undecided.

The results come as Paxton and Cornyn remain locked in a bitter primary runoff, and the pollsters said Talarico's lead is likely due, at least partially, to the ongoing GOP battle. No Democrat has won a statewide election in Texas in three decades.

"While the Democratic candidate leading two established Republicans in these match-ups is sure to raise some eyebrows," they wrote, the results "reveal a Republican electorate still registering the effects of the months-long, bruising, negative campaigning by Paxton and Cornyn, and the GOP divisions the race has exacerbated." _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/b79d2526-cad0-40d0-a914-9805b86d0cda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" TX-18 Democratic primary runoff: Christian Menefee vs. Al Green"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/5bba6904-85c6-4ab7-886e-df1b8215cc6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Gabby Birenbaum** - In this rare clash of sitting incumbents, Houston Democratic Reps. **Al Green** and **Christian Menefee** are squaring off after the Legislature consolidated their two Houston districts, both long represented by Black Democrats, into one during last summer's redistricting.

**" Future of Texas hemp uncertain in THC fight: 'We're all still very anxious and nervous'"** via [KXAN Austin](https://substack.com/redirect/d645e685-76f2-4a3e-8e89-6de9111a76a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Adam Schwager** - The immediate future of the Texas Hemp industry likely rests in the hands of Travis County District Court Judge **Daniella Deseta Lyttle**. The hemp industry has asked Judge Lyttle to grant a temporary injunction against the enforcement of new Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) rules -- which they claim will shutter the industry. The rules first went into effect on March 31, but were later halted by a temporary restraining order which expires on May 1.

If Judge Lyttle grants the Texas hemp industry the injunction? "We'll expand on our THC product line. We're actually having a conversation about having a third location if this goes through," Happy Cactus co-owner **Todd Harris** said. "We're all still very anxious and nervous."

If the order is denied it would result in skyrocketing licensure fees and the ban of intoxicating hemp flower, which Harris says makes up 70% of his sales. And instead of opening a new store, he might have to close one. "This [east Austin] location and how it survives and thrives is very much tied to how the injunction and what happens in that courtroom," Harris said.

In the courtroom, the Texas Hemp industry called two witnesses to the stand: Galveston-county based hemp store operator **Kenneth Burner** , and Texas Hemp Business Council (THBC) Executive Director **Mark Bordas**. Burner, an Iraq veteran, highlighted his practice of employing those who've either served in the military or as a first responder. **" Dallas' Highland Park votes to leave Texas' second-largest public transit system"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/b14709f7-502e-4221-873f-f1c87beb7584?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Joshua Fechter** and **Colleen DeGuzman** -- Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the state's second largest public transit agency, fractured Saturday as voters in one suburb chose to leave the transit system.

Voters in Addison and University Park also weighed in on proposals to leave the system but chose to remain in the agency. This leaves 12 cities connected through DART.

Seven Union Pacific cars derailed early on April 23 as a 230-car train rounded a sharp curve near West Third and Bowie streets in the Seaholm District. No one was injured, but the incident snarled traffic for hours and delayed school bus routes in West Austin as crews worked to clear the scene.

The train was transporting "mixed commodities" rather than hazardous chemicals, but Brown -- a longtime passenger rail advocate who oversees emergency management in his role as county judge -- said the cars could just as easily have been carrying something far more dangerous, like chlorine.

The praise for the speedy response was rare for the Austin Police Department, which has struggled for years with slow response times and regularly faces online criticism and complaints. The rapid intervention also raised a question: Is the Police Department getting faster?

An American-Statesman analysis of median response times over the past decade shows that the swift reaction to the Buford's Bar shooting was an outlier. Since the city's police oversight agency began categorizing grievances in 2022, the most common type has been "no assistance," which includes slow responses and alleged no-shows. _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/929d5837-38a4-475b-9d60-09f69bdebd3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

TOP NEWS " Exclusive: Texas teacher accused of molesting student was on 'do not hire' list" via ' Bayliss Wagner - Youths walk by the windows of the dining hall on their way to lunch in 2006 at the Giddings State School in Giddings, Texas. When one of their teachers was arrested and accused of repeatedly molesting an eighth-grade student last fall, Elgin school district officials expressed shock. "Accusations such as these are concerning, and if proven to be true, unacceptable," the Austin-area district told KVUE in November, noting they had moved quickly to assist police when the claims were made against Turran Fennix. But it wasn't the first time that Fennix, 34, had been accused of having inappropriate interactions with a child, according to records obtained by Hearst Newspapers. Two years earlier, Texas' juvenile justice agency barred Fennix from future work in the system after he was caught giving a skin-to-skin back massage to a student in a dorm room, a clear policy violation. Administrators determined he should be fired for the incident, but allowed him to resign instead. Elgin Middle School hired him just a few months later. Fennix's previously unreported trajectory from the Texas Juvenile Justice Department to a middle school raises questions about how thoroughly Elgin vetted the employee and whether the state disclosed his full background. () " As the state targets cities over ICE policies, Austin considers next steps" via Mose Buchele - In some ways, Texas has provided a crystal ball for the rest of the country when it comes to immigration policy. Before the Trump administration poured billions into immigration enforcement and built partnerships between local police and state and federal immigration agents, Texas was already doing it. So, for those opposed to the deportation surge, Texas is worth paying attention to. That was one of the takeaways from a panel Saturday at the KUT Festival. "Kristin Etter , the director of policy and legal services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, said, "Here in Texas, we have kind of a four- to five-year head start when it comes to the rest of the country. We have operated a program called Operation Lone Star that has used state resources. So we have a model here in Texas for this police/ICE collaboration." Another takeaway from the panel: In a state where much of the voting public and all state political leaders support aggressive immigration enforcement, opposition becomes local. In liberal Austin, local leaders have tried to craft policies that would limit police partnering with ICE, but the governor took notice and the Austin Police Department had to soften one policy under threat of funding cuts. City Council Member Zo Qadri said Austin still has tools at its disposal "to make sure that folks are protected and are safe." City Council Member Jos e Velasquez pointed to millions in city funding for local immigration advocacy groups and the council's support for Austin's "safe to call" initiative as examples. () " Tornado in North Texas Destroys Several Buildings and Displaces Residents" via Jesus Jim enez - The whir of chain saws and the beeping of utility trucks were the most prominent sounds around Mineral Wells, Texas, on Wednesday afternoon, after a tornado the previous night ripped through a section of the city. In one industrial sector of Mineral Wells, a town of about 15,000 residents west of the Dallas-Fort Worth area, roofs had been sheared off buildings and other structures had been reduced to piles of what looked like matchsticks. But the destruction appeared limited to an area of commercial properties that were largely empty. Most residential homes in the area were unscathed, and no deaths were reported, though at least five people were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries and many residents were displaced, city officials said. Christopher Hester , 33, said that he was sitting in his living room with his wife on Tuesday afternoon when their front door suddenly burst open. He said they immediately took cover in the hallway of their home. () " High gas prices eating into Texans' budgets, fueling inflation" via Cobler andColleen DeGuzman - The large signs outside of gas stations across Texas intended to catch drivers' eyes are lately doing so for all the wrong reasons. At a Valero gas station in Edinburg, Reynaldo Zarazoa , who installs tile for a living and has to haul tools and equipment around in his gray GMC pickup, watched Thursday as the display on the gas pump reached $78 -- nearly a fifth of his weekly income. "My work is cheap and the gas is expensive," said Zarazoa, a father of two living in Peñitas, a small city in the Rio Grande Valley. "But I have to drive every day, every day for work." The price of fuel has risen significantly since the U.S.-Israel war on Iran began on Feb. 28, closing a key international shipping lane for oil and gas, the Strait of Hormuz. The average price for a gallon of gas in Texas was $2.55 in early February, according to AAA. It had risen to $3.78 on Wednesday morning. () " Court sides with 'EPIC City' developers over state agency in fair housing fight" via Nick Wooten - "This ruling confirms what we have maintained from the beginning -- that Community Capital Partners has been willing, ready, and committed to following Texas law at every step," said Imran Chaudhary pictured above at the EPIC City project site outside of Josephine. A Travis County judge has ordered a state agency to comply with the fair housing agreement it made with the developer of a Muslim-centric neighborhood in North Texas. The Texas Workforce Commission must abide by the terms of a September 2025 settlement it reached with developer Community Capital Partners. The group is behind The Meadow, previously called EPIC City. The 201st District Court issued the injunction Tuesday. A judge also denied the state's request to dismiss the case on Wednesday, allowing Community Capital Partners' lawsuit to move forward. () 2026 " Republican Brett Ligon, former Montgomery County DA, wins special election for Texas Senate seat" via Texas Tribune'sAlejandro Serrano and Colleen DeGuzman -Brett Ligon, the Republican former district attorney of Montgomery County, won a special election Saturday for the state Senate district vacated by Brandon Creighton , who was tapped last year to be chancellor of the Texas Tech University System. Ligon defeated Democrat Ron Angeletti , an educator and small-business owner who was the only other candidate on the ballot. The two are set for a rematch in November for a full four-year term. In the meantime, Ligon will serve the remainder of Creighton's term, which runs until the start of the next legislative session in January. "The voters of SD4 have delivered a clear message tonight. Conservative values and Republican dominance in Texas are alive and well," he said in a statement declaring victory 25 minutes after polls closed. "Democrats from Texas and all over the country threw everything they had at us. Democrat politicians were here today in full force, campaigning hard for my opponent. As if we had been flying the 'Come and Take It' flag - they tried - and they failed." Senate District 4 - which spans across Chambers, Harris, Jefferson, and Montgomery counties - voted for President Donald Trump by a 34-point margin in 2024, making it one of the reddest seats in the upper chamber. It is considered a virtual lock for Republicans in November, even with midterm political headwinds that have left Democrats optimistic about flipping GOP legislative seats. () " 'It's a mess': With no Trump endorsement in Texas Senate race, Cornyn and Paxton are locked in an expensive brawl" via Patrick Svitek - Nearly two months ago, President Donald Trump promised he would make an endorsement "soon" in the Republican primary runoff for US Senate in Texas. That endorsement still has not arrived -- and its absence is keeping the race highly competitive. Three people involved in the race said they no longer expected Trump to get involved in the battle between Sen. John Cornyn and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. However, they cautioned he could change his mind before the May 26 runoff, keeping both sides on edge in the final weeks. While Democrats haven't won statewide in Texas since 1994, they have a Senate nominee in state Rep. James Talarico who is energizing liberals ahead of the November midterms and raising massive sums. Republicans long wanted to avoid a damaging runoff that could make things easier for Talarico, in part by having Trump boost one candidate and pressure the other to back down. Trump was likely to eventually endorse Cornyn after he and Paxton advanced from a March 3 primary, sources told CNN at the time. However, Trump grew frustrated after Republican operatives leaked his expected plans, the sources said. Trump also fielded calls from some of his most ardent supporters, pushing him not to endorse Cornyn and warning it would be a mistake with his "Make America Great Again" base. () " Talarico leads Cornyn, Paxton in Senate matchups, UT poll finds" via Benjamin Wermund - James Talarico , a Texas Democratic primary candidate for U.S. Senate, leads both Republicans vying to face him in the November U.S. Senate contest, according to a new poll released Wednesday. Talarico led U.S. Sen. John Cornyn 40% to 33% in a potential matchup, and held a 42% to 34% advantage over Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , the University of Texas at Austin's Texas Politics Project survey found. In both cases, 19% of voters said they were still undecided. The results come as Paxton and Cornyn remain locked in a bitter primary runoff, and the pollsters said Talarico's lead is likely due, at least partially, to the ongoing GOP battle. No Democrat has won a statewide election in Texas in three decades. "While the Democratic candidate leading two established Republicans in these match-ups is sure to raise some eyebrows," they wrote, the results "reveal a Republican electorate still registering the effects of the months-long, bruising, negative campaigning by Paxton and Cornyn, and the GOP divisions the race has exacerbated." () " TX-18 Democratic primary runoff: Christian Menefee vs. Al Green" via Gabby Birenbaum - In this rare clash of sitting incumbents, Houston Democratic Reps. Al Green and Christian Menefee are squaring off after the Legislature consolidated their two Houston districts, both long represented by Black Democrats, into one during last summer's redistricting. The runoff pits the Texas delegation's newest member, Menefee, 38, against one of its longest-tenured -- the 78-year-old Green. With the two candidates largely aligned on policy, the race has turned on each of their fighting styles and whether voters prefer Green's congressional experience and protests against Donald Trump or Menefee's millennial energy and history of waging legal battles with Texas Republicans. The two do have differing stances on cryptocurrency, with Green a skeptic and Menefee more willing to embrace the industry as it spends lavishly in support of his candidacy. Texas' 18th Congressional District has a majority Black voter population and is one of the deepest blue seats in Texas. Long a bastion of Black political power -- past representatives include Barbara Jordan , Craig Washington and Sheila Jackson Lee -- it was left without representation for nearly a year after Rep. Sylvester Turner died in office in March 2025. Menefee led the November special election and won the January runoff to finish out Turner's term. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Dan Patrick eyes closing 'gambling loophole' for prediction markets. The feds stand in Texas' way." via Texas Tribune's Ayden Runnels - In March, Lt. Gov.Dan Patrick directed state senators to explore ways to close "gambling loopholes" that allow online prediction markets to operate in Texas, raising concerns that state elections and sporting events could be manipulated for profit. Patrick's directive was the first time a state leader officially acknowledged the existence of rapidly growing prediction markets, which let users wager on outcomes tied to anything from the weather to election winners and sports scores. Any attempts by the Texas Legislature to restrict prediction operators, however, would run into federal roadblocks as the Trump administration insists that oversight belongs to a U.S. agency, not the states. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has taken vigorous steps to retain exclusive regulatory oversight, suing to block five states from taking legal action against predictive markets, including a lawsuit filed Tuesday against Wisconsin. () " Future of Texas hemp uncertain in THC fight: 'We're all still very anxious and nervous'" via Adam Schwager - The immediate future of the Texas Hemp industry likely rests in the hands of Travis County District Court Judge Daniella Deseta Lyttle. The hemp industry has asked Judge Lyttle to grant a temporary injunction against the enforcement of new Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) rules -- which they claim will shutter the industry. The rules first went into effect on March 31, but were later halted by a temporary restraining order which expires on May 1. If Judge Lyttle grants the Texas hemp industry the injunction? "We'll expand on our THC product line. We're actually having a conversation about having a third location if this goes through," Happy Cactus co-owner Todd Harris said. "We're all still very anxious and nervous." If the order is denied it would result in skyrocketing licensure fees and the ban of intoxicating hemp flower, which Harris says makes up 70% of his sales. And instead of opening a new store, he might have to close one. "This [east Austin] location and how it survives and thrives is very much tied to how the injunction and what happens in that courtroom," Harris said. In the courtroom, the Texas Hemp industry called two witnesses to the stand: Galveston-county based hemp store operator Kenneth Burner , and Texas Hemp Business Council (THBC) Executive Director Mark Bordas. Burner, an Iraq veteran, highlighted his practice of employing those who've either served in the military or as a first responder. "Tells us something about their character right from the beginning," he said. () " Commissioners accept financing deal for new baseball stadium that gives the county a park" via Biediger - The decisions made during negotiations between Bexar County Commissioners and Missions baseball owners have been mostly behind closed doors -- until now. On Tuesday during Commissioner's Court, the officials agreed to a kind of trade with Designated Bidders, revealing something of how that deal will be structured. The agreement approved by commissioners gives the county two parcels of land for a park near the San Pedro Creek Cultural Park in exchange for restructuring the financing agreement it made with the team's ownership group in 2024 to build a new downtown ballpark. At the same time, county officials agreed to release its portion of the tax increment guarantee from the Houston Street Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone, which is estimated to make up 14% of the total ballpark project cost. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Powerful North Texas transportation leader fired after 35 years on the job" via Rachel Behrndt \-- Michael Morris , a longtime regional official who oversaw hundreds of billions of dollars of transportation projects, was fired from his position after 35 years on the job, officials said. The firing followed a months-long fight and a weeks-long court battle that pit two powerful government entities against each other over the firing and has now led TxDOT to propose a new agreement clarifying which group has the power to terminate the official, according to documents reviewed by WFAA. Morris served as the Director of Transportation for the North Central Texas Council of Governments (NCTCOG) for 35 years, according to a statement from the organization. His last day on the job was April 28, 2026, the statement reads. "We are grateful for his more than 40 years of service to the region, including 35 years of leadership that helped shape one of the nation's most dynamic transportation systems," the statement reads. () " Dallas' Highland Park votes to leave Texas' second-largest public transit system" via Joshua Fechter and Colleen DeGuzman -- Dallas Area Rapid Transit, the state's second largest public transit agency, fractured Saturday as voters in one suburb chose to leave the transit system. Highland Park will pull out of DART, according to election returns Saturday. It's the first time any city has pulled up its stake in the agency since 1989 when Flower Mound and Coppell opted to leave. Voters in Addison and University Park also weighed in on proposals to leave the system but chose to remain in the agency. This leaves 12 cities connected through DART. Nearly 70% of voters in Highland Park decided to discontinue DART in the town, according to final but unofficial returns. The result was mirrored in Addison, where 70% voted to remain connected to the system; University Park was more narrowly divided, with 54% voting to stay. () " After Austin train derailment, calls grow to move freight rail out of downtown" via Alex Driggars - A freight train derailment in downtown Austin last month is prompting Travis County JudgeAndy Browwn to renew calls to move a major rail line out of the city's urban core -- a long-debated idea that has yet to gain traction. Seven Union Pacific cars derailed early on April 23 as a 230-car train rounded a sharp curve near West Third and Bowie streets in the Seaholm District. No one was injured, but the incident snarled traffic for hours and delayed school bus routes in West Austin as crews worked to clear the scene. The train was transporting "mixed commodities" rather than hazardous chemicals, but Brown -- a longtime passenger rail advocate who oversees emergency management in his role as county judge -- said the cars could just as easily have been carrying something far more dangerous, like chlorine. "Chlorine can cause a cloud of chlorine gas, and that would be a horrible thing," Brown said. "Just the fact that you're potentially carrying hazardous chemicals right through this huge metro area with condos literally feet away from where this curve was is not great." () " Is APD really 'quiet quitting'? Critics raise concerns as response times lag" via Austin Sanders and Karina Kumar - Last month, Austinites and officials alike heaped praise on the Austin Police Department after officers responded to a mass shooting on West Sixth Street in 57 seconds and took down the gunman minutes later. The praise for the speedy response was rare for the Austin Police Department, which has struggled for years with slow response times and regularly faces online criticism and complaints. The rapid intervention also raised a question: Is the Police Department getting faster? An American-Statesman analysis of median response times over the past decade shows that the swift reaction to the Buford's Bar shooting was an outlier. Since 2017, response times - while seeing some improvement in the last year under Police Chief Lisa Davis - have lagged even as 911 call volumes have decreased. The findings are reflected in public complaints. Since the city's police oversight agency began categorizing grievances in 2022, the most common type has been "no assistance," which includes slow responses and alleged no-shows. () " A solar surge in Austin: New projects target reliability and climate goals" via Chaya Tong - Austin is betting on solar power as it confronts a growing energy crunch, approving a slate of projects aimed at boosting local generation and cutting reliance on the broader ERCOT grid. The City Council recently approved three proposals designed to expand that local capacity: a new solar facility on a closed city landfill, solar installations across city facilities and negotiations for up to 40 megawatts of battery storage in partnership with local manufacturer Base Power, Inc. Austin Energy spokesperson Matt Mitchell said the initiatives would add about 78 megawatts of capacity -- enough energy to power nearly 20,000 homes for a year -- and the agreement with Base Power offers comparable value to the 100 megawatt Jupiter battery contract the council approved last July. Mitchell said the utility was already 73% carbon-free last year, offsetting 65% of customer demand, and argued that expanding local generation helps stabilize costs by reducing the need to import power during extreme weather and peak demand. () " San Antonio psychiatric hospital laying off nearly 650 employees" via O 'Neill - Laurel Ridge Treatment Center on the far North Side plans to lay off 648 employees starting in June, after the federal government terminated its Medicare and Medicaid coverage. After losing its Medicare and Medicaid funding, San Antonio's Laurel Ridge Treatment Center is planning to lay off hundreds of employees. "As a result of this regulatory action, we must implement a workforce reduction," Ashley Sacriste , CEO of Laurel Ridge, said in a statement. The hospital is "deeply disappointed by this outcome and recognizes the significant impact it will have on our dedicated team members and the communities we serve," she added. () " A Houston ISD exec tapped for Beaumont schools superintendent during its second state takeover" via Sneha Dey - Texas officials again tapped a Houston schools administrator to helm a state takeover, this time for Beaumont ISD. Sandi Massey is the new state-appointed superintendent of Beaumont ISD as the district has struggled with years of poor academic performance. Massey comes from the nearby Houston ISD, where she was the chief of schools during a takeover that has been controversial among parents but lauded among state leaders. "I know what it takes to transform a district," Massey said at a press conference Wednesday. "I am ready to do it here in Beaumont and make this city the best instruction you've ever seen." Massey is the third Houston schools official tapped in recent weeks to help shepherd a state takeover. Texas Education Agency commissioner Mike Morath appointed Ena Meyers , who was a Houston ISD chief, as superintendent of Lake Worth ISD last week. And Peter Licata , on his first day on the job as the state-appointed superintendent of Fort Worth ISD, hired another Houston ISD chief Daniel Soliz as his deputy. () BUSINESS NEWS " D-FW's GameStop bids $56 billion to buy iconic internet auctioneer eBay" via Brian Womack - GameStop is proposing to acquire eBay in a deal that would bring one of the bigger names in Internet history under a North Texas-based company. The Grapevine-based retailer said it submitted a non-binding proposal to acquire the Silicon Valley e-commerce company for $125 per share, according to a GameStop statement. The aggregate undiluted equity value is approximately $55.5 billion. The proposed offer is comprised of 50% cash and 50% GameStop common stock. The North Texas company has built a 5% economic stake in eBay through derivatives and beneficial ownership of stock. GameStop -- known in some circles more for its "meme stock" days and a push into Bitcoin -- could be making a significant move with the proposed acquisition. The company, which has been shuttering stores where it sells video games, consoles and collectibles, saw its sales decline in the previous fiscal year though it swung to an operating income from a loss. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
BREAKING: Today I’m co-leading a coalition of more than 20 states in urging the U.S. Supreme Court to protect access to mifepristone, a safe and effective abortion medication.
On Friday, a federal court of appeals reinstated a medically unnecessary requirement that mifepristone be dispensed in person. That ruling is NOT supported by science, would create administrative chaos across the country, and would undermine states’ ability to protect access to reproductive care.
Soon after we filed our amicus brief, the Supreme Court granted an administrative stay, temporarily pausing the lower court’s ruling until next Monday. I strongly urge the Supreme Court to issue a final ruling that protects the availability of mifepristone through telehealth, making it easier for women, especially in rural, low-income, and underserved communities, to access reproductive health care.
Bottom line: mifepristone is a safe, effective, and lifesaving medication, and attempts to limit access to it are driven by a right-wing, anti-science political agenda determined to chip away at reproductive freedom nationwide.
As Attorney General of California, I will never stop fighting to protect reproductive freedom for every single Californian — because reproductive rights are human rights.
If you’re with me, I’m asking you to step up and power this work with a contribution of whatever amount you can afford today. You can give by clicking this link or on the buttons below. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

name: bishforcongress.com
subject: Christine Bish Has a Plan to Fix California’s Wildfire Insurance Crisis
body:
[ View in browser](https://m4s4f.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/mr/sh/WCPxRrNLV1LtwSCEGcqYZQVm93Fhn2uH/kNjDUxW_TIA5)

**Christine Bish Announces the WILDFIRE Act to Restore Insurance Access and Protect California Communities
========================================================================================================**

I’m announcing my plan to fix California’s wildfire insurance crisis.

I want to share something important with you today. I am officially announcing the WILDFIRE Act.

A comprehensive plan to stabilize California’s collapsing wildfire insurance market, restore access to coverage for homeowners, and reduce long term disaster costs.

The reality is this: in wildfire country, insurance is not optional. It is survival.

Right now, too many families across our district are losing coverage, facing massive premium increases, or being pushed into expensive, limited plans that do not fully protect them. Entire communities are at risk of becoming uninsurable, and that threatens not just homeowners, but property values, mortgages, and local economies.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We cannot keep waiting for the system to fix itself. It will not.
-----------------------------------------------------------------

That is why I developed the WILDFIRE Act. The Wildfire Insurance and Loss Defense, Federal Intervention and Risk Enhancement Act to create a national framework that actually works.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Wildfire Act is the Plan to Fix California’s Wildfire Insurance Crisis
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
This plan establishes a National Wildfire Insurance Program, administered by the Treasury and FEMA, to provide reliable baseline coverage. It includes a federal backstop for catastrophic losses, but only after private and state systems are exhausted, ensuring accountability and protecting taxpayers.

Just as importantly, this plan is built with discipline and transparency. It uses premium based participation, requires repayment mechanisms, and rewards homeowners who take steps to reduce risk through mitigation efforts like defensible space and fire resistant construction.

This is not about expanding government for the sake of it. It is about restoring a functioning private insurance market while making sure families are not left without options.

The urgency is real here in our district. Communities like El Dorado County, Truckee, South Lake Tahoe, Grass Valley, and Penn Valley are on the front lines of this crisis. People are doing everything right and still losing coverage.

[ That is unacceptable.](https://m4s4f.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/WCPzyXJTZ6uvfh6CvvTeS466g94v5105/KwvRK4V-uotv)

The WILDFIRE Act takes a different approach. Instead of reacting after disaster strikes, it prepares before it happens. It brings stability back to the market, gives homeowners clarity, and reduces long term costs for taxpayers.

Within 180 days, this plan puts rules in place. Within one year, it launches a pilot program in high risk areas like ours. Within three years, it expands nationwide with full congressional oversight to ensure it works as intended.

This is a serious problem, and it deserves a serious solution.

The current system is failing families. My plan is designed to fix it.

But I cannot take this fight to Washington alone.

If you believe we need real solutions, not empty promises

If you believe families deserve access to reliable insurance

If you believe it is time to protect our communities before disaster strikes.

[ I am asking you to stand with me.](https://m4s4f.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/WCPzyXJTZ72ijjJTI0xKDoFtovy2KicD/yD4kd_3xInCe)

Together, we can bring this plan to Congress and deliver real results for the people who need it most.

Thank you for your support,

Christine Bish

Candidate for Congress, CA-03

**Meeting with Local Leaders**
------------------------------
Christine Bish met with local leaders this week at the Chamber of Commerce to talk about one issue that keeps coming up again and again: wildfire insurance.

From small business owners to insurance agents and community leaders, the message was clear. The current system is not working.

Policies are being dropped. Costs are rising. And communities are being left behind.

That is exactly why Christine is fighting for the WILDFIRE Act a real solution to restore access to insurance, stabilize the market, and protect families and businesses before disaster strikes.

These conversations matter. Because real solutions come from listening to the people living it every day.

**bishforcongress.com**

8121 Golden Vista Way, 95843, Antelope

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com.

You've received this email because you've subscribed to our newsletter.

[Unsubscribe](https://m4s4f.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/un/v2/sh/WCPxRrWByckTj8nTRQetzL09AeXc94sL/DbPfcKeCvu_9)

The conversations I’ve had are heartwarming. Our state is full of good, hardworking people who are struggling to get by. But together, we’ll get California back on track.

I’m so grateful for people like Dana who are powering this campaign. I’ve never taken a dime of corporate PAC money. I rely on grassroots supporters like him to keep us going.

body:
Today you have a very special chance to stop the Hollywood groomers who are turning our children and grandchildren against us and the Godly values we love.

| | | You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.
---
| |
---
| | Dear Friend in Faith,Please – for the sake of all our families – take it from me as someone who’s lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with “entertainment” that grooms children.You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace.But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue’s Clues_...

# West Virginia Deserves Better **— **
# 7 Days Until the Republican Primary

---
|
---
|
---
| |
Dear Friend,

People ask me why I’m running for the U.S. Senate.
Here’s the truth:
**Because Washington isn’t working for West Virginia anymore.**
Too many politicians go there to build power—
Protect their position—
Take care of themselves.
**That’s not me.**
I spent **26 years serving this country as a Green Beret.**
I’ve **built businesses right here in West Virginia.**
I’ve lived under the same regulations and pressures you deal with every day.
I know what it’s like to meet payroll.
To deal with government overreach.
To fight to keep costs down.
**Career politicians don’t.**
**They talk about problems—I’ve lived them.**
I’m running because West Virginia needs a U.S. Senator who understands real life—not just Washington.
**Someone who will fight for:**
* **Securing the border and enforcing our laws**
* **Defending life and our constitutional rights**
* **Protecting the 2nd Amendment and religious freedom**
* **A balanced budget to tackle our national debt**
* **Investing in West Virginia infrastructure—roads and water systems**

And lowering costs for working families by:
* Limiting the size of government
* Cutting unnecessary regulations
* Promoting free-market competition

**Not more bureaucracy.**
**Not more control.**
**Not more of the same.**

* * *

If you want someone who will serve—not rule—
**VOTE TOM WILLIS — MAY 12 PRIMARY**
**Early voting ends Saturday, May 9**
**7 DAYS LEFT**
Together, we can bring real leadership back to West Virginia.
**It’s Time for a Change, West Virginia.**
Sincerely,
**Tom Willis**

# Tuesday, May 5, 2026

It's Election Day, everybody! I hope everyone has a plan to go vote today.
Tonight, I'll be going live around 7:45 after the polls close.
You can watch at **[theangrydem.com](https://substack.com/redirect/f84f049b-5303-455b-9ac7-9e73f8c62c97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , **[theangryohioan.com](https://substack.com/redirect/8b913bf6-c25a-45c1-ad17-0e5e4b1a327a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , or on **[Facebook](https://substack.com/redirect/842b44cd-479e-4293-be28-cd3584d03537?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , **[YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/8c54683b-3cfd-4807-a095-678b152964ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , and **[X](https://substack.com/redirect/28c5a9ca-88de-483d-928a-a1f04d21ab2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
I'm just going to be hanging out, watching the results come in, giving my comments, and maybe having a few guests swing by as the night unfolds.

* * *
Below, I'll include some resources that may help you before you head to the polls.
Google your county name and "Board of Elections." Your local board of elections usually has everything you need, including polling locations, sample ballots, candidate lists, and basic voting information.
**[https://www.waynecountyoh.gov/](https://substack.com/redirect/54a5461f-7865-4278-9520-978d5c9d97d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[https://www.boe.ohio.gov/ashland/](https://substack.com/redirect/dc3c83b2-f012-47a9-be38-29d8bcfc85c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[https://www.boe.ohio.gov/medina/](https://substack.com/redirect/b193df46-2d2f-4bc3-9c5a-94a036e42df5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
**[https://boe.cuyahogacounty.gov/](https://substack.com/redirect/8bf8adc0-69af-4b36-b350-0d7eda43574d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And please, take a few minutes to look at your sample ballot before you go.
Know who is actually running in these races. Do not just walk in and let the first name you recognize make the decision for you.
There are candidate lists available, and **[Vote411 from the League of Women Voters](https://substack.com/redirect/d7ca026c-9e26-4440-ad57-a05b27ea39fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** is another great resource. It can show you polling **locations, sample ballots, candidate information** , and what you need to bring with you to vote.
**It may be raining, so take an umbrella**.
The best times to go are usually outside the rush hours.
Avoid before work, lunch, and right after work if you can.
If you go during one of the random slower parts of the day, you will probably be in and out.
And honestly, this is a midterm primary, so it should not be anything like waiting in line during a presidential year.
* * *
### The Statewide Races I'm Watching
The first race I'm watching is the Republican primary for governor.
**Vivek Ramaswamy** is the endorsed GOP candidate, but **Casey Putsch** , also known online as **[Casey the Car Guy,](https://substack.com/redirect/ec092658-9086-480f-b75b-b05e56d0f69e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** has been getting a lot of support on social media. He has not raised a ton of money, so the question is whether that online energy actually translates into votes.
I do not think the real question is whether Vivek wins. I think the real question is how much he wins by. That margin will tell us something about how real the online grassroots energy around Casey actually was, and the actual popularity of Vivek.
* * *
The **attorney general** race between **[Elliot Forhan](https://substack.com/redirect/61d2a809-8192-47f7-a370-739374494593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[John Kulewicz](https://substack.com/redirect/9f01fb01-b086-4044-a180-0d998b70e3ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. John is the endorsed Democratic candidate, and Elliot has some baggage. I do not know if everybody knows the actual stories behind Elliot Forhan's baggage, but to be perfectly honest, it seems like some of it was overblown and turned into a smear campaign. He definitely has people who strongly support him, but I do not know if that will be enough to overcome the Democratic endorsement.

subject: An excellent way to honor a mom this Mother’s Day
body:
But not every woman will experience Mother’s Day that way.

| | | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkcGK3DAMhp9GuWVQ7Ik9OeSwNAQKTaEstMegtbUZQ2wH25Ptvn3JkD7A3iT9P_-HpD_TPJFbXVh-kufe7G5OeabAfw2vK4fyQZ8l3mOIiXz0s0ChamxrbA9fU9neWCVFxX2jte60RrxV9942eNVEVqKw8ialUfatfTeoqBMor6Zy_ZGELbYNSkR9MbbD7p2FYcPNrWO44mOzVDhfTAyZ007F7exCiEcVw8VEX639vZQtg3wBMYIYF7fzZUv8FtPTAGI8OxCjj-XOKdeWPkGO2YAcpuEFW6Fep9cfIBT5AnIQNxBqySAHCiDUo_g5x0cyDHLYUswbm-LCckqerXt4kAN7cus5NOQ3cksAOZzQg3lqMRQOB2hq5l-6_vb7e_3_FlXq7fbh1tVlpeGKy5H5XLR8_TV7L_4FAAD__yZYnSg)

Friend of Life, This Mother’s Day weekend, many people will call their moms, sit around a table together, or take a moment to remember the woman who gave them life. In those moments, it becomes clear just how much of who we are has been shaped by someone who chose to step into motherhood, even when it required sacrifice, patience, and strength. **But not every woman will experience Mother’s Day that way.** Right now, there are women sitting alone, trying to decide if they will become mothers at all. Everything around them is telling them to move quickly, to decide before they have time to process what’s happening, before they have space to ask questions, before they have ever seen the life they carry. Some of them are sitting in their cars, staring at the doors in front of them, telling themselves this is the only way forward, even though something inside them keeps asking them to wait just a little longer. **[And if nothing interrupts that moment, the decision will be made in minutes.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkcGK3DAMhp9GuWVQ7Ik9OeSwNAQKTaEstMegtbUZQ2wH25Ptvn3JkD7A3iT9P_-HpD_TPJFbXVh-kufe7G5OeabAfw2vK4fyQZ8l3mOIiXz0s0ChamxrbA9fU9neWCVFxX2jte60RrxV9942eNVEVqKw8ialUfatfTeoqBMor6Zy_ZGELbYNSkR9MbbD7p2FYcPNrWO44mOzVDhfTAyZ007F7exCiEcVw8VEX639vZQtg3wBMYIYF7fzZUv8FtPTAGI8OxCjj-XOKdeWPkGO2YAcpuEFW6Fep9cfIBT5AnIQNxBqySAHCiDUo_g5x0cyDHLYUswbm-LCckqerXt4kAN7cus5NOQ3cksAOZzQg3lqMRQOB2hq5l-6_vb7e_3_FlXq7fbh1tVlpeGKy5H5XLR8_TV7L_4FAAD__yZYnSg)** That is why PreBorn! exists. Because when a woman is given the chance to see her baby on an ultrasound, something begins to change. The screen lights up. The heartbeat fills the room. What once felt distant suddenly becomes real in a way she cannot ignore. For the first time, she is no longer choosing in fear or pressure, but with clarity. And more than 80% of women choose life in that moment. Months later, she is not carrying the weight of a decision she cannot undo or wondering what might have been. She is holding her baby. **[This Mother’s Day, there is no more meaningful way to honor a mom in your life than by helping another woman become one.](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyUkcGK3DAMhp9GuWVQ7Ik9OeSwNAQKTaEstMegtbUZQ2wH25Ptvn3JkD7A3iT9P_-HpD_TPJFbXVh-kufe7G5OeabAfw2vK4fyQZ8l3mOIiXz0s0ChamxrbA9fU9neWCVFxX2jte60RrxV9942eNVEVqKw8ialUfatfTeoqBMor6Zy_ZGELbYNSkR9MbbD7p2FYcPNrWO44mOzVDhfTAyZ007F7exCiEcVw8VEX639vZQtg3wBMYIYF7fzZUv8FtPTAGI8OxCjj-XOKdeWPkGO2YAcpuEFW6Fep9cfIBT5AnIQNxBqySAHCiDUo_g5x0cyDHLYUswbm-LCckqerXt4kAN7cus5NOQ3cksAOZzQg3lqMRQOB2hq5l-6_vb7e_3_FlXq7fbh1tVlpeGKy5H5XLR8_TV7L_4FAAD__yZYnSg)** $28 provides one ultrasound, and that single moment can change everything. name: Dan Cox
subject: Your electric bill didn’t have to be this high.
body:
Maryland families are paying more—and it’s fixable.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/coxforcongress/something-happened-this-week-6754053?e=5bb5efcda7)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

,
Maryland families are paying some of the highest electric bills in our region—and it didn’t have to be this way.
While states like Virginia and West Virginia continue to produce more of their own power, Maryland has become increasingly dependent on energy from outside the state. At the same time, demand is rising fast, especially with the growth of data centers across the PJM grid.
The result? **Higher costs for you.**
And it’s about to get worse.
More in-state power plants are scheduled to shut down in the coming years, which means even less local supply and even more pressure on prices.
We don’t need to accept that.
I have a plan to bring costs down and restore energy stability in Maryland:
* Bring reliable power generation back online where possible
* Expand cleaner natural gas capacity and modernize existing infrastructure
* Advance small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs)
* Require large-scale energy users, like data centers, to carry more of their own load

This is about one thing: **lowering your electric bill and protecting Maryland families from rising costs.**
If you’re ready for a different direction, **join me today at**[**DanCoxforGovernor.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/12eBlnkiTPj?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)
I’d be honored to earn your vote.
