# [Data just made Palantir worth $250B - is this #1 software company next?](https://substack.com/redirect/3873cd74-8b0a-40d4-8987-648ddf07519a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3873cd74-8b0a-40d4-8987-648ddf07519a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Palantir just rocketed to **[$250 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by helping companies extract value from user data.
The big data gold rush is here**,** but **[the company that stands to profit the most may not be Palantir...](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* A new disruption to smartphones gives users a share in the data profits, already facilitating +$1B in earnings and generating +$115M in revenue.
* With**[32,481% revenue growth](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**,**** this company is gearing up for a possible Nasdaq listing (stock ticker: **[$MODE](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**), and pre-IPO shares are available at only $0.50/share.

It's a $1 trillion industry, and their disruptive _EarnPhone_ is now being distributed by Walmart and Best Buy.
**[The time to secure your spot at $0.50/share is now!](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Click here to learn more](https://substack.com/redirect/4861bc8c-6f1c-4e99-8f08-a0c1ceefaa92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
Armstrong's email may give a nod to efficiency gains, **" adjusting our cost structure now so that we emerge from this period leaner, faster, and more efficient for our next phase of growth"** and while that may well be true it's not the whole story. Coinbase is not Spirit Airlines. The firing of 700 people is not an attempt to save the company from a crisis. Cost savings always matter in business but being positioned for the future is more important and the managerial class is being wiped out in corporate America by AI. Not because they are particularly bad at their jobs, but because it just makes better business sense to use AI.
## [A future without customers? The AI boom's hidden flaw](https://substack.com/redirect/ac76c6d4-dc62-4b78-b725-60c0f7a47e43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[](https://substack.com/redirect/ac76c6d4-dc62-4b78-b725-60c0f7a47e43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

The timing is particularly stark. Coinbase is making these cuts at the same moment the CLARITY Act is moving toward passage on Capitol Hill. That legislation, if passed, will finally bring regulatory clarity to digital assets and is widely expected to unlock much broader institutional adoption of crypto. On the corporate and industry side, the future of Crypto looks brighter than it has in years. Yet none of that good news was enough to save those 700 jobs. The AI revolution doesn't wait for regulatory tailwinds. It moves whether the policy environment is ready or not.

This pattern is going to repeat itself again and again across the economy. Companies, even the best ones, even the ones at the cutting edge, are going to start quietly auditing their workforce against what AI can now do. Every department, every process, every role, will be stress-tested. The ones where AI can perform as well or better than a human will be pruned. The humans who remain will be those who can direct, manage, and augment the machines rather than compete with them. Coinbase is not an outlier. It is simply one of the first major, visible examples.
Brian Armstrong is not afraid to ruffle feathers (as the CLARITY Act negotiations demonstrated.) His email to employees was blunt, almost clinical. He explained the dual forces at work: a still-volatile crypto market and the accelerating capability of AI. The company is choosing to act early and deliberately rather than wait until it is forced to. That may be the responsible leadership thing to do, but it is painful for those affected and the wider industry ramifications hint at a volatile future. If Coinbase is making these decisions, how many other firms like Coinbase are on the cusp of making these same decisions? It is interesting to note that Coinbase's share price leapt 4% in pre-market trading just minutes after Armstrong's tweet.
The broader lesson is uncomfortable but undeniable. AI is not coming for low-skill jobs first. It is coming for the jobs that involve analysis, coordination, reporting, and decision support, exactly the kind of knowledge work that many college-educated professionals assumed would be safe. Coinbase's cuts are a warning shot across the bow of the entire white-collar economy.
## [The "Ghost economy" is becoming very real](https://substack.com/redirect/e8b7f26a-5a42-4494-be1d-4b2be335fb35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

We've been told that AI would create more jobs than it destroys. That may still prove true in the very long run. But in the short and medium term, the destruction is real, visible, and happening at some of the most innovative companies in the world. Coinbase isn't laying people off because it is struggling. It is doing it because it sees a future where fewer humans can achieve more.
This is the new reality.
The Coinbase decision will be painful for the people leaving, but the company itself is between a rock and a hard place. Companies that want to remain competitive in an AI-driven world are going to have to make hard choices about headcount. The ones that move fastest and most decisively will have the advantage. The ones that pretend this isn't happening will eventually be forced to catch up under much worse conditions. That is the real reason that Armstrong acted how he did, when he did.
The rest of corporate America is watching. Many know that all too soon they will face the same choice.
The AI revolution isn't just coming. It has already arrived and it is taking names, even in the most cutting edge of business.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. I saw what you did to my grandpa and we aren’t going back.
| | | | | [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001NTfqRgAC38JLWNCJLOMlfQrym_w20h41wv5YADwM4Wcx60_zITYEjttUn9TKj9cPgIOQpWmo4mulnWw9DJHohmuT_JqO5F6HHnLOL5E6zmrdEmAM_VGRs6Nuzpw0c0zkk2yEpRU332Yn9XCxJR43OzRMRW8EYc8A47b9huHRHZhOsfdlNyIzYdtmKSaTCIarfKp1-y2BZmpNlzsr7W6XmM0J5JqAjj-7&c=csxMtY5XwPYjERdVy5QBBD9HzCOZEZxkd3bAdCrzS8WX8ikeBQ7E2A==&ch=RPgP5xm6t_HOWUmt_cPv1uC_LeaCAobWsWs6UF8Or4y6lBJIrRzeHQ==)
---
Peter, Late on the night of Wednesday, April 29th, word began circulating that MAGA was set to declare a state of emergency to cancel Louisiana's May 16th election.
In the days that followed, the distinction was made that the GOP was only canceling Congressional elections and not the other elections, including ours, set to take place on May 16th.
However, after hundreds of conversations between voters and our field team this weekend, it's clear that the damage has been done. Voters are throwing away their absentee ballots and canceling plans to vote under the false assumption that the election has been canceled.
---
| [](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001NTfqRgAC38JLWNCJLOMlfQrym_w20h41wv5YADwM4Wcx60_zITYEjttUn9TKj9cPgIOQpWmo4mulnWw9DJHohmuT_JqO5F6HHnLOL5E6zmrdEmAM_VGRs6Nuzpw0c0zkk2yEpRU332Yn9XCxJR43OzRMRW8EYc8A47b9huHRHZhOsfdlNyIzYdtmKSaTCIarfKp1-y2BZmpNlzsr7W6XmAXhzhZ_WMzP&c=csxMtY5XwPYjERdVy5QBBD9HzCOZEZxkd3bAdCrzS8WX8ikeBQ7E2A==&ch=RPgP5xm6t_HOWUmt_cPv1uC_LeaCAobWsWs6UF8Or4y6lBJIrRzeHQ==)
---
Quick history lesson: The KKK Act of 1871, bans the underhanded tactics used by the Ku Klux Klan to disenfranchise black voters during the Reconstruction era, and to this day remains a foundational tenet of American civil rights law.
One of the segregationists' favored methods of ensuring newly emancipated black voters did not exercise their right to vote was by placing ads in local newspapers advertising erroneous dates for upcoming elections or false claims that elections had been postponed or canceled.
That is exactly what is happening in Louisiana right now.
Within a week, MAGA has reintroduced Jim Crow-style gerrymandering to disenfranchise black voters, and now they are using old-school tactics to trick black/Democratic voters into not voting in a critical election.
My message to MAGA is this: As a descendant of sharecroppers, I saw what you did to my grandpa, and we aren't going back.
This is why our campaign is joining up with the other Louisiana Democratic campaigns targeted by the GOP's assault on voters and is preparing to do what my ancestors did and challenge these segregationists in court.
This is money we should be spending on GOTV efforts; however, we cannot allow MAGA to get away with this. This is a dry run for canceling the midterms, and we either stop them here or canceling elections becomes the norm.
[We need a torrent of support from across the nation to make up for the massive hole that has been blown in our budget by this unfolding legal effort. Please, can you rush a donation of $25, $10, or even just $5 to help ensure our campaign can mount this legal challenge whilst keeping our voter contact efforts intact?](https://r6msg8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001NTfqRgAC38JLWNCJLOMlfQrym_w20h41wv5YADwM4Wcx60_zITYEjttUn9TKj9cPUP14WGGjaFfDEFzAk-6hSKq-74X9ZX0Uog0SmhguHrszfz_PH5HZM68uSAj5NFgO2a1w6f9-KLYX3sHH9SgkKtvGT7PHNS5DuXd_yeIfZd47u-OZMeYNwGFXBJeHqN9r6PuqosZnKUGGhaK_XyK8CxFUSAILsL8G0iqGzM0niPjuvwo90yUtNg==&c=csxMtY5XwPYjERdVy5QBBD9HzCOZEZxkd3bAdCrzS8WX8ikeBQ7E2A==&ch=RPgP5xm6t_HOWUmt_cPv1uC_LeaCAobWsWs6UF8Or4y6lBJIrRzeHQ==)

body:
It’s why I stood up to Trump in 2020

|
---

| | _This is a longer message than I usually send. I hope you’ll give me a moment to explain why your urgent donation to my campaign for governor of Georgia is so important. If you don’t have time to read to the end, but would like to donate, you can do that _[**here**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130802067/618966203/985402107?firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&zip=18326&phone=&employer=&occupation=&amount=25&refcode=EM_RTI_GD_20260505_FR_5C_T1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA3MDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjgxYjQ1NjYtYWI0OC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2K7nROCU15yhA4awOmiSnRN6pF8Moye_H_Vsi9tONwQ=)_._

My wife, Brooke, and I have raised our three boys with a family motto: Doing the right thing will never be the wrong thing. It’s helped us navigate a lot of tough situations together over the years.

**When I was Georgia’s lieutenant governor, doing the right thing was standing up to Donald Trump.**

I was one of the only elected Republicans who refused to go along with Trump’s lies when he tried to steal the 2020 election. The president attacked me online, his followers sent my family death threats, and our kids were bullied at school.

In the heat of that moment -- with our house surrounded by state troopers -- one of my sons put this wooden coaster on my desk, reminded me of our family motto, and told me, “I’m proud of you.” | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130802072/618966206/985402107?firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&zip=18326&phone=&employer=&occupation=&amount=25&refcode=EM_RTI_GD_20260505_FR_5C_T1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA3MDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjgxYjQ1NjYtYWI0OC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2K7nROCU15yhA4awOmiSnRN6pF8Moye_H_Vsi9tONwQ=)
---

Speaking at the DNC and campaigning for Kamala Harris was also doing the right thing. So was deciding to run for governor as a proud Democrat so we can bring transformative change to our state.

**As governor, I promise I’ll always do the right thing for Georgia. But I can’t win without your help.**

_[**Will you donate to my campaign right now? Election Day is just two weeks away, so anything you give will help fund our urgent voter outreach.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130802075/618966209/985402107?firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&addr1=&city=Cresco&state=PA&zip=18326&phone=&employer=&occupation=&amount=25&refcode=EM_RTI_GD_20260505_FR_5C_T1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA3MDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjgxYjQ1NjYtYWI0OC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2K7nROCU15yhA4awOmiSnRN6pF8Moye_H_Vsi9tONwQ=)_

Your support means the world to me.

Geoff

courts alone. He has accomplices.

19 Senate Democrats have joined Republicans in helping advance judicial
crony nominees who should have been stopped cold — clearing the way for
more right-wing judges with lifetime power over our rights.

That should outrage every one of us.

The courts are where our biggest fights are decided: voting rights,
reproductive freedom, workers’ rights, corporate accountability, and
democracy itself.

And Trump knows that.

That’s why he and his allies are turning the judiciary into a political
weapon, packed with loyalists who protect the powerful at everyone else’s
expense.

hold senators accountable — including the 19 Democrats helping make this
possible — and mobilize grassroots pressure to stop dangerous
confirmations before they become lifetime appointments.

fail to stop makes Trump’s court-packing scheme harder to undo.

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn't born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she's gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina's legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she's running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who's walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she's been one of President Trump's fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left's sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She's not here to make friends. She's here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina's Income Tax--the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think--not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she's ready to do what she's always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

clean_body: Can you spare a minute to let me tell you why it’s paramount that we keep fighters like Mike Carey in Washington? | Fellow Conservative, You’ve known me for a long time. You know that I am a firm believer in small, limited government and the "America First" agenda that puts hardworking families ahead of the DC swamp. You also know that in my world, your word is your bond. Whether I’m fighting in the deep swamp or standing up for our constitutional rights, I follow through on my commitments. It’s a simple concept, but one that the radical Left seems to have abandoned years ago. I’ve seen plenty of people come and go on Capitol Hill. Some are just there to warm a seat, and others—mostly across the aisle—are there for the wrong reasons entirely. But every so often, you meet a true patriot who is there to do the work. Mike Carey is exactly that kind of leader. | Mike isn't just a colleague; he’s a friend and a rock-solid conservative. As a veteran and a devoted family man, Mike understands the stakes of the fight we are in. He has been a critical partner of mine in Washington, working to dismantle the deep state and rein in the reckless spending that has squeezed the pockets of every Ohioan. We cannot afford to lose Mike’s voice in Congress. While the media and the Democrats are pouring millions into Ohio to try and flip his seat, we need to make sure he has the resources to fight back. Investing in battleground districts like the 15th is the only way we protect our House majority and keep the momentum of the Trump administration moving forward. In a town full of talkers, Mike Carey is a doer. He doesn't back down, he doesn't flinch, and he never forgets who he represents. He asked me to reach out to my most trusted supporters—people like you—to help him cross the finish line. The Democrats want nothing more than to take back the House and stall our progress. name: Wes Moore
subject: I’ll cut to the chase
body:
We’re back in the game, but we have a lot of ground to make up.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1360%2E1086043%2EuOgfT1)
Peter, you’re a critical part of this team. That’s why I wanted to personally give you an update on the state of our playing field.
**Here’s a real time update on where things are at:**
[****](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260505-1.OE_MCM&refcode=em-20260505&t=2&akid=1360%2E1086043%2EuOgfT1)
Most people don’t know this, but Maryland law requires public officials like me to stop fundraising while the legislature is in session.
For months, I’ve been focused solely on winning results for Marylanders including:
* Protecting our immigrant community,
* Investing in public safety,
* Lowering Marylanders' energy bills,
* Increasing our housing supply,
* _And more._

_But we didn’t raise a single dollar._ We’ve had to wait. You know who hasn’t? **Republicans.** While we were hard at work, they were raising money nonstop from Donald Trump’s donors.
**And now, they’re about to flood Maryland with dark money.**
[**Can I count on you to chip in today to help support our campaign, Peter? I don’t take it lightly asking for your help, but we really need to close this gap.**](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260505-1.OE_MCM&refcode=em-20260505&t=3&akid=1360%2E1086043%2EuOgfT1)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260505-1.OE_MCM&amount=5&refcode=em-20260505&t=22&akid=1360%2E1086043%2EuOgfT1)**
This seat has flipped parties between every governor for the last twenty years. I flipped it from a Republican — and now Donald Trump’s allies want to flip it right back. It’s why Maryland is one of Republicans’ top targets in 2026.
I say, the pattern stops with me, Peter. I refuse to let this seat turn red. We need strong Democrats who aren’t afraid to fight back against Trump in state leadership positions, _now more than ever._
[**So I'm personally asking you: will you please chip in whatever you can right now?**](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260505-1.OE_MCM&refcode=em-20260505&t=23&akid=1360%2E1086043%2EuOgfT1)
— Wes

I think Democrats are at our best when we trust our voters.
The people we seek to represent know what they're living through. They can decide what leadership they need. Our job is to trust them.
That's why it was so frustrating to watch party insiders at the DCCC step into competitive primaries this week and try to narrow the field before voters cast their ballots.
I know there are people who will call that "strategy," but to me it really feels unbelievably dismissive towards the people who make up our party, you know, the actual voters.
This is the kind of politics we have to move past.

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi RMV friends!
Big news today—we’re announcing several Freedom Fest **Friday** speakers 👀 Want to be the first to know who made the lineup? You’ll need to be on the priority list. [Sign up now so you don’t miss the reveal.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Plus, we did a video all about Freedom Fest! [Check it out.](https://link.email.joinrmv.) Here's your summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are weighing [new insurer fees to cover a $140 million shortfall](https://link.email.joinrmv.)—raising concerns about higher premiums—while a bipartisan transparency bill for government officials advances, but [will likely be vetoed](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Meanwhile, a proposed [“Right to Know” amendment was blocked](https://link.email.joinrmv.) from the ballot over single-subject rules.
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** [Grid changes](https://link.email.joinrmv.) are driving increased gas use and even a return to coal amid reliability concerns, as debate continues over [shifting away from natural gas](https://link.email.joinrmv.) despite widespread reliance. Wildlife policy, wolf compensation, and prairie dog conservation are [on the agenda for CPW](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while a [Front Range rail plan faces funding uncertainty](https://link.email.joinrmv.) tied to legal and ballot challenges. At the same time, [small business optimism is rising](https://link.email.joinrmv.) with increased lending and investment.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage/Commentary Spotlight...** A bipartisan majority [opposes animal testing](https://link.email.joinrmv.) even as federal funding continues, highlighted by the release of 1,500 dogs from a research facility. Public health debates are also intensifying, with a former advisor [questioning vaccine and COVID-era policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while commentary points to [deepening political divisions](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and rising concerns over partisan hostility shaping national discourse.

This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, May 5, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Rail plan on the brink: Court ruling and ballot fight could kill funding](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
On April 29, Governor Jared Polis declared in a press release that Colorado had struck a deal to bring passenger rail to the Front Range — three daily round trips between Denver and Fort Collins, launching in 2029, with no new taxes.
“At nearly half the cost of previous studies,” he wrote, “this agreement proves that through partnership and collaboration, passenger rail service across the Front Range is not a far-off dream, but a reality.”
The day before, RTD’s board voted to authorize $5.58 million from its FasTracks savings account and support the project’s preliminary funding framework. The term sheet itself was executed April 30 between the Colorado Transportation Investment Office (CTIO), a government-owned enterprise within CDOT, and BNSF Railway.

* **Record funding fueling small business growth:** The SBA delivered a record $45 billion in loans to over 85,000 small businesses last year, alongside a $53 billion investment portfolio supporting expansion, hiring, and job creation.
* **Optimism remains above historic averages:** Small business confidence has stayed above its 52-year average for 12 of the past 13 months, signaling strong expectations for continued growth and investment.
* **Pro-growth policies credited for momentum:** The article attributes gains to tax cuts, deregulation, and a focus on Main Street, arguing these conditions are helping entrepreneurs expand operations and strengthen local economies.

* **Commentary warns of rising political hostility:** The piece argues that intense opposition to former President Trump has fueled impeachment efforts, legal challenges, and broader partisan conflict.
* **Claims legal system and public discourse are being shaped by bias:** It points to hundreds of ongoing legal cases and public narratives following recent events as examples of what it describes as politically driven actions.
* **Call for unity rooted in American founding principles:** Drawing on Thomas Paine, the article frames today’s political divide as an internal struggle over freedom, urging Americans to reject division and reaffirm core constitutional values.

| | Peter, Kathy Hochul just announced she is "working with the Legislature to change New York's redistricting process." **Translation** : She wants to throw out the state constitution, gut the Independent Redistricting Commission that New York voters approved in 2014, and let Albany Democrats draw congressional maps that hand themselves more seats. _**_She's already done it once._**_ In 2024, New York Democrats got a court order to redraw maps mid-decade — after stacking the Court of Appeals to do it. The goal was to pick up five seats for Democrats. They got four. _**_Now she wants to do it again!_**_ Make no mistake, Peter, when Hochul talks about "leading the fight for voting rights," what she actually means is rewriting the rules so Democrats win seats they cannot win at the ballot box. If you believe in fair maps, the answer is not "fight fire with fire." The answer is to put the fire out. But I cannot win that fight in Washington if I lose this seat in November. And Hochul knows it. Every dollar she helps raise for the Democrats running against me in NY-17 is a dollar invested in the same gerrymandering scheme. clean_body: She wants to redraw the maps. Again. | | | | = | | Peter, Kathy Hochul just announced she is "working with the Legislature to change New York's redistricting process." Translation : She wants to throw out the state constitution, gut the Independent Redistricting Commission that New York voters approved in 2014, and let Albany Democrats draw congressional maps that hand themselves more seats. She's already done it once. In 2024, New York Democrats got a court order to redraw maps mid-decade — after stacking the Court of Appeals to do it. The goal was to pick up five seats for Democrats. They got four. Now she wants to do it again! Make no mistake, Peter, when Hochul talks about "leading the fight for voting rights," what she actually means is rewriting the rules so Democrats win seats they cannot win at the ballot box. If you believe in fair maps, the answer is not "fight fire with fire." The answer is to put the fire out. But I cannot win that fight in Washington if I lose this seat in November. And Hochul knows it. Every dollar she helps raise for the Democrats running against me in NY-17 is a dollar invested in the same gerrymandering scheme. = | | | = | | Mike Lawler Congressman NY-17 | | = | | | = | | | | | | USE THE ADDRESS BELOW TO CONTRIBUTE BY CHECK** LAWLER FOR CONGRESS PO Box 137 Chappaqua, NY 10514 | Paid for by Lawler for Congress, Inc. | | =

name: Jen Kiggans
subject: I apologize for asking again
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kiggans for Congress
body:
Not what I spent my time doing

| | | | |
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDUwNV85MS1YSy4xMTAxMTdfdDE4ODk0NDAtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA1MDVfOTEtWEsuMTEwMTE3X3QxODg5NDQwLTIwNjgifQ/kkmsAztU8N1Gp67S24_lIA)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDUwNV85MS1YSy4xMTAxMTdfdDE4ODk0NDAtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA1MDVfOTEtWEsuMTEwMTE3X3QxODg5NDQwLTIwNjgifQ/wZKCLYYfdVe0UYGL-KYcEQ)
I know things are tight right now. I see it at the grocery store just like you do. But if you can spare even $5 to help keep a Navy Vet and a Nurse Practitioner in this fight, it would mean the world to me.

Peter, we
wanted to share a quick story from the campaign trail that reminded us
exactly what’s at stake in this race.

At a recent event in Westland, a woman stood up to talk to Abdul. She
said:

“I’ve worked in a hospital for 21 years, and I have seen the change. These
people cannot afford healthcare. I’m a union person, so my health care is
locked in. But I just want to say you're real, you're for the people, and
you've got my vote for sure.”

She's spent over two decades watching patients come through hospital
doors, and can clearly see how broken the system is.

And she’s not alone.

Across Michigan, we’re building a coalition of people who are tired of
watching the status quo fail them. They’re ready for someone who will
fight for real change and a government that actually supports working
people.

That’s exactly what Abdul is fighting for. He’s the only candidate in this
race who supports Medicare for All — because nobody should have to rely on
luck or a union contract just to get the care they need.

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: The rioters walked
body:
The cop who stopped them didn't
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=6d1f9e69e9c94169b6733c142fd1cec4&_e=ZEubeyMbMnxNEfJjLgNnCaC2-S0aiIxDdq4EJP5ki3aJ6AgdGE012XQzAHPRYURg5ikQU52SE6IoqmyuqtP0TxKzKFtO3sTcU5eqvxkzlNRbGrVaQcd8vaVQGtTtZc_aaDgIF1rpziKYuiOtplLhMop9-2Gc1fvdWk_iocNe-O0QiDnrF1O7NO_rKqjUkPwsQgln-4VOoiLJI-rR0NxbVmvgn024Qw1aofIDHYiYkv7pLfDw2n2NWpTHC9cLRXVZLnRTR3v1XTPSIOCC2P3Mt7u5jcEFO5Lolpuw-utjDGjH9qafe9n5rsMc-arpU2bYKCblZIPDnuNOFU0gRLlfECmlqVVe8UQ92hLB4nMCxI8He29IbYfi4oagJLN2gFNZkDDVXNymDQpfSjOkJsb05P7xa7GyDcbHrAaCnlAhTp5-w_p-XJlS7_lzCy5TCf8y) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.
The National Center for Police Defense is standing with Jeff and his family — funding his legal defense and providing support while this ordeal drags on. But we cannot do it without you.

They want to lock him away for using non-lethal bean bag rounds against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party. I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed. It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse. On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused. Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway. Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence. That's it. That's the "crime." Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted. This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets. And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for years with no end in sight. The National Center for Police Defense is standing with Jeff and his family — funding his legal defense and providing support while this ordeal drags on. But we cannot do it without you. I'm asking you to . $25. $50. $100. Whatever you can. Your gift goes to Jeff's defense and to supporting his family through this nightmare. Stand With Officer Teng Today Your gift funds Jeff's legal defense and supports his family through this nightmare. 100% of your donation goes toward Officer Teng's legal defense fund. The radical left is counting on your silence. They want you to think this is just one officer, one city, one story. It isn't. If they can prosecute 20+ officers for stopping a riot with non-lethal force, no officer anywhere is safe. Jeff Teng showed up. He held the line. He protected his partner, his city, and the rule of law — with every tool he was authorized to use. The least we can do is show up for him. Don't look away. Share this with every law enforcement supporter you know. And please, For Jeff. For every officer they're coming after next. Sincerely, Sheriff Joe Arpaio Former Sheriff, Maricopa County, Arizona Honorary Supporter, National Center for Police Defense P.S. Officer Jeff Teng is facing felony charges for stopping a riot. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260505_nowvsthen_actrs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260505_nowvsthen_actrs]
Peter,
The political moment we’re in right now is not the same as it was two years ago.
People are paying attention in a different way. They’re seeing who’s really fighting for them, and who’s taking millions from AIPAC and other Republican-funded groups. And let’s be clear about what we’re up against:
Over $2 million was spent on a single candidate in New Jersey, and more than $21 million was poured into races in the Illinois primary.
That’s the playbook. Flood the airwaves. Drown out grassroots voices. Buy the outcome.
And there’s no doubt they’re going to try it here in St. Louis, too, because they did it to me last cycle. Outside groups poured $15 million into defeating me and installing their hand-picked opponent—all because I fight for my community, stand up to Trump’s agenda, and pushed forward legislation to force a ceasefire in Gaza.
I don’t answer to AIPAC. I answer to the people.
St. Louis deserves a fighter: someone who will stand up for families, tell the truth even when it’s hard, and never back down just because powerful interests don’t like it. I’ve been that fighter in Congress before. And when I’m back, I’ll be that fighter again.
And look, we don’t need to outraise them dollar-for-dollar.
We have the right message: Working to ensure our basic needs are met, standing in solidarity with the people of Palestine, and fighting back against Trump’s agenda.
And people are aware and supporting the movement. We just need to organize, get our ads out, and make sure we cut through the noise they’re paying millions to create.
Now that our fundraising numbers have been made public—and you can bet right-wing groups are already combing through them, deciding where to pour in millions to try to control the outcome of this election, drown out our voices, and buy a result that doesn’t reflect our community.
Please contribute $25 or whatever you can today, before our deadline, so we can show AIPAC and all the other groups betting against us that we’re in this fight to win it. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-26q2?refcode=x_260505_nowvsthen_actrs&amount=25]

Cori

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: James and I don’t let Republicans push us around
body:
I’m proud to share the Democratic ticket with James.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
My grandmother would always tell me, _“No te dejes.”_ Don't let them push you around. **Fight back.**
That’s the spirit driving this campaign and what’s driving the Democratic ticket this year.
I’m running for Governor to end Greg Abbott’s corruption tax on working Texans and deliver the basics our families deserve. And I’m proud to share this ticket with James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, who is ready to take the same fight straight to Washington.
If we win together, we can do something Texas hasn’t seen in a long time. We can build real power to lower costs, protect public schools, and stop Republicans from using our state as their personal piggy bank.
**[Will you split a donation between me and James Talarico right now to help us compete everywhere and win this November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260505_1_talarico.NvleyR&refcode=em20260505-1060&amount=5&t=1&akid=1060%2E299639%2E3qfbv8)**
[Split a Donation »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260505_1_talarico.NvleyR&amount=5&refcode=em20260505-1060&t=2&akid=1060%2E299639%2E3qfbv8)
Here's what I know about James: he's an eighth-generation Texan and a former middle school teacher who flipped a Trump district because he knew how to talk to people who'd been left behind.
He's been standing beside me in Austin, fighting the billionaire mega-donors who have bought our state legislature and turned it against working people. **Now he's ready to take that fight to Washington.**
The reality is that the biggest threat we face isn't each other — it's the people at the very top who spend billions to keep us angry and divided. Abbott, Cornyn, Paxton... _all_ of them AND their donors are counting on us to stay divided. **They’re counting on Texas Democrats to run out of money, run out of fight, and run out of hope.**
_Not this time._
We don’t need to match them dollar for dollar. But we do need the resources to organize, communicate, and compete in every corner of Texas. When we run strong top-of-ticket campaigns, every Democrat down the ballot runs stronger too.
**So if you’re ready to fight for a Texas where every child can go to a great public school, every family can afford health care, and our government works for people instead of billionaires,[will you split any amount today between my campaign and James?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260505_1_talarico.NvleyR&refcode=em20260505-1060&amount=5&t=3&akid=1060%2E299639%2E3qfbv8)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260505_1_talarico.NvleyR&amount=5&refcode=em20260505-1060&t=22&akid=1060%2E299639%2E3qfbv8)
James and I are both Texans. We both know this state can be better. And we both know that the only way we win is together.
Thank you for supporting both of our campaigns,
Gina Hinojosa

name: Roger Lau
subject: Exclusive state-of-the-race update for Derek
body:
---
Derek, Roger Lau here. As one of our most engaged supporters, it’s important to me that we keep you updated on the work that the DNC is doing to take back control of Congress — and the work we still have to do. **So today I’m writing to you with an exclusive midterm strategy memo.** \--------------------------------------------------
**Date:** May 5th, 2026
**Subject:** EXCLUSIVE: State-of-the-Midterms Update Democrats have a real chance at winning back control of both the House and Senate this November. Outlined below is a roadmap to Democratic Congressional majorities.
* **To win the Senate,** we need to hold open Democratic seats in Michigan, Minnesota, and New Hampshire, and defend Jon Ossoff’s seat in Georgia. We need to flip seats in North Carolina, Alaska, Maine, Ohio, and Texas — electing Roy Cooper, Mary Peltola, Graham Platner, Sherrod Brown, and James Talarico.
* **To win the House majority, Democrats may only need to win _two_ of the sixteen toss-up races this November.** If we won all sixteen, we’d likely have a 14-seat advantage in the House.
* **GOP megadonors and super PACs are dumping hundreds of millions of dollars into these races to ensure that they retain control.** They know that if Democrats win control of Congress, their Republican rubber stamps will be effectively powerless for the next two years.
* **But Democrats are fighting back.** We’re hiring hundreds of new organizers who will register tens of thousands of new Democrats in key battleground states. We’re investing in state parties, sharing our DNC Playbook, and hosting trainings to ensure that campaign staff on the ground have the knowledge, tools, and resources they need to run winning campaigns.

\-------------------------------------------------- So, Derek, I’m asking: If this update was helpful, and if winning back Congress matters to you, [**please make a $7 contribution to the DNC today. On Saturday, our redwood community gathered at the National AIDS Memorial Grove in San Francisco for _Take Me to the Trees_ —a night inspired by the collective, enduring power of the redwoods. As dusk descended on the canopy, forest lovers came together in colorful style to celebrate what is possible when we show up for the places and people we love. From cocktail hour in the grove to an artful dinner under the night sky, from an energetic live auction to a groovy silent disco, this sold-out event brought new and old friends together in a magical way (yes, there was a magician). **Together, we raised $1 million to continue reviving the redwood range.** Our community's incredible generosity powers our work to protect redwood lands, restore forests, and ensure equitable access for everyone. These USPS postmark changes are just the latest step taken by MAGA's vote suppressors to limit mail-in ballots.
Why? Because in recent elections, the percentage of people voting by mail hasn't favored their extremist candidates, and voter participation has actually increased via the use of vote-by-mail and drop boxes. This all leads to candidates MAGA doesn't like winning elections.
Team, these changes are about who has power now and how badly they want to keep it. RUSH $35 or more right now to help inform voters of this change and defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050526_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=050526_2&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.

Because in recent elections, the percentage of people voting by mail hasn't favored their extremist candidates, and voter participation has actually increased via the use of vote-by-mail and drop boxes. This all leads to candidates MAGA doesn't like winning elections. Team, these changes are about who has power now and how badly they want to keep it. RUSH $35 or more right now to help inform voters of this change and defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [] Voter Action Project [] HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [] Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media. Team, Every voter needs to know about this massive change. The Supreme Court just handed Republicans a dangerous new opening to gerrymander congressional maps across the country — weakening one of the most important protections in the Voting Rights Act.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130814549/619003320/789508428?refcode=260505_RG_scotus&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzOTFiNzllZi1jNjQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lsUZYz32ASjjHzptYCEM8rXDwxOKmNOIL2bysP0x9TA=)
**This is how Republicans hold onto power: Not by winning voters, but by rewriting the rules.**
And let’s be clear about what this means: They can now dilute Black and Latino voting power, manipulate lines in swing districts, and rig control of the House before a single ballot is cast.
This is about power. And Republicans are willing to undermine our democracy to keep it.
Before today, Republicans were desperately looking for ways to change the battlefield, defy the odds, and keep control of the House — and the Supreme Court just handed them the best gift they could ever imagine.
**[That’s why we need to fight back against their anti-democratic extremism stronger than ever before. [DONATE NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130814551/619003322/-309737922?refcode=260505_RG_scotus&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzOTFiNzllZi1jNjQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lsUZYz32ASjjHzptYCEM8rXDwxOKmNOIL2bysP0x9TA=)

Peter — Have you heard the latest? James Uthmeier is hiding. No, seriously. Jose Javier called Uthmeier the **_most corrupt Attorney General we’ve ever had and challenged him to a debate to prove it._** But Uthmeier is nowhere to be found. So we want to know: **Should James Uthmeier stop hiding and face Jose Javier on the debate stage?** | | | [YES](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130814971/619004902/-944744615?refcode=em_JJR_FR_DebateChallenge_050526&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWFhZmJlZTMtYzg0OC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=uc8k9WawCj2GjKvV8CiB1_jkM3cpRMvvPOkD_WrkDXw=&emci=20f9856f-b148-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=9aafbee3-c848-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=32374386) | [NO](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130814972/619004903/-944744615?refcode=em_JJR_FR_DebateChallenge_050526&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWFhZmJlZTMtYzg0OC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=uc8k9WawCj2GjKvV8CiB1_jkM3cpRMvvPOkD_WrkDXw=&emci=20f9856f-b148-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=9aafbee3-c848-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=32374386)

Uthmeier has no problem chasing headlines or talking tough when the cameras are on. But when it comes time to defend his record in front of the people of Florida? Silence.
And honestly, can you blame him? Here's what he'd have to answer for:
_❌ The $10 million Hope Florida scandal — money meant for Medicaid recipients that ended up in political committees tied to him._
_❌ Sitting on his hands while FPL pushed through the largest utility rate hike in U.S. history._
_❌ Wasting hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars on political stunts like Alligator Alcatraz._
_❌ Taking $100,000 from UF Law to teach one course, two hours a week._
Unlike Uthmeier, Jose Javier believes Floridians deserve to hear directly from the candidates running for the highest law enforcement office in our state. He's not afraid to defend his record of fighting crime, taking on corruption, and standing up to the powerful interests driving up our costs.

subject: Polls are about to close in Ohio

body:
Hey, it's Sherrod. I promise I wouldn’t be reaching out if it weren’t so important.

The primary here in Ohio is coming to a close, and we’re running out of time to replenish our critical resources before the start of the general election. Polls are about to close, and as soon as this race is called, we’re preparing for a spike in Republican spending against me.

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOSH GOTTHEIMER FOR CONGRESS
body:
---
| | Team,

Josh is fighting to put parents back in control of what their kids can access online.

Piers Morgan and Geraldo Rivera teamed **[up to take Adam Mockler down a notch](https://substack.com/redirect/284ac0ba-5b8b-4d48-a191-d26b91a7c32c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after his disrespectful stunt on CNN getting in Scott Jennings' face.
"Don't be a wise ass!" Geraldo snapped at the Trump-hating Youtuber.

This is what happens when a coddled brat faces real men in political debate. Arguments and rhetoric aside, respect and humility is key and Mockler has neither.
The 23-year-old Meidas Touch podcaster thought he could **[nag and push Scott Jennings without consequence](https://substack.com/redirect/308c7aff-488c-4d5b-825f-69b0a65f5393?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and found out real quick why personal boundaries matter.
But disrespecting Geraldo and his career like this is a new low. I'm glad to see how both Piers and Geraldo decided they could not let his comment stand and humbled him on the spot **[(watch above).](https://substack.com/redirect/284ac0ba-5b8b-4d48-a191-d26b91a7c32c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Mockler strikes me as someone who hasn't been slapped in the face by real life and lives primarily in online spaces, just based on his behavior and demeanor. Despite his large audience he lacks the wisdom and experience to be taken seriously by adults and thinks his way to the top is by agitating people and hunting for virality.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e708ae9-2f73-47d2-a860-f94f1c09d2a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

In early 2026, the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps launched a series of unprecedented strikes against American data centers in the Middle East, targeting Amazon Web Services facilities in Bahrain and an Oracle data center in Dubai. Iran justified these attacks by claiming that these facilities hosted AI systems used by the U.S. military for intelligence analysis and war simulations. For the first time, hyperscale cloud infrastructure--previously considered civilian technology--had become explicit military targets in a regional conflict.

These attacks mark a dangerous evolution in warfare. Data centers, the backbone of the digital economy, are increasingly being recognized as dual-use infrastructure with strategic military value. As the U.S. and its Middle Eastern partners rush to build AI capabilities, they have inadvertently created high-value targets within missile range of adversarial states. The vulnerability of these facilities demonstrates how the physical infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence has become inextricably linked to national security.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=196571184&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk2NTcxMTg0LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgwMTg2OTUsImV4cCI6MTc4MDYxMDY5NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.-ybKvHeg_ZVrEK1FNjJJOf5kdeA6Fj-8izzNd_XOjok)
Yet as policymakers grapple with these geopolitical threats abroad, an equally complex challenge is emerging at home. Across America, local communities are mounting their own resistance against data center expansion--not with missiles, but with zoning laws, protests, and regulatory opposition. The irony is striking; while Iran attacks data centers for being too close to military operations, American communities are fighting them for being too close to homes, schools, and environmental resources.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9664d7af-9cb7-4fe7-976d-1f04e084810d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The primary battleground is water. Large AI data centers can consume up to five million gallons of water daily--the equivalent of a small town--to cool the massive server farms that power artificial intelligence. In water-stressed regions from Arizona to Arkansas, residents are increasingly asking why scarce local resources should be diverted to quench the thirst of tech giants. In Little Rock, protesters recently rallied against a proposed Google facility, citing concerns that data center water consumption would drain local lakes and wetlands over the long term.

Noise pollution compounds the tension. Cooling systems and server fans generate constant industrial hums that disrupt wildlife, alter animal behaviors, and disturb human sleep patterns. In Chandler, Arizona, the city council unanimously rejected a proposed AI data center in late 2025 due largely to noise concerns raised by nearby residents.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.ZEbrXMuMNZTvxODijouH276P_LlYrjVNLmLRhPFx--U?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196571184)
Perhaps most ironically, some communities are now opposing data centers precisely because of the military targeting risks revealed by Iran's attacks. Facilities located near military bases--previously seen as secure locations--are now viewed by some residents as potential magnets for foreign strikes or sabotage operations. National security assets have become neighborhood liabilities.

The convergence of these pressures creates a precarious moment for American AI infrastructure. The nation is simultaneously racing to expand data center capacity to compete globally while facing opposition from the very communities expected to host them. As Iran demonstrated, data centers are no longer invisible pieces of internet infrastructure; they are contested sites of geopolitical and environmental conflict. Whether they can survive foreign missiles abroad and local opposition at home remains an open question--and one that will shape the future of artificial intelligence development.

**Data Center Footprint** :

\- Average data center: Around 100,000-150,000 square feet (about 2-3 acres)
\- Hyperscale data centers: About 435,000 square feet (10 acres) or larger
\- Latest trend (2025): New AI-focused data centers average about **613,000 square feet**--nearly 14 acres per facility
\- The buildings themselves are typically massive warehouse-style structures, 2-3 stories high, packed with server racks
**Military Base Footprint** :

\- White Sands Missile Range (NM): The largest U.S. military installation at approximately **3.2 million acres** (~139 billion square feet)
\- Joint Base Lewis-McChord (WA): 414,000 acres (~18 billion square feet)
\- Fort Bliss (TX): ~1.1 million acres (~48 billion square feet)
\- Fort Hood (TX): ~214,968 acres (~9.4 billion square feet)
\- Even "smaller" major bases like Fort Bragg are 160,000+ acres (~7 billion square feet)

A single typical Army division installation covers roughly 15,000-40,000 acres--equivalent to about 150-400 average data centers just in land area.

To put it another way: The largest military bases are tens of thousands of times larger than data centers. You could fit the entire data center campus for a major tech company inside many military bases and still have room for live-fire training ranges, airstrips, and maneuver areas.

This massive difference explains why data centers often seek locations near military bases for perceived security advantages, while occupying a fraction of the physical footprint.
Undersea internet cables face multiple serious threats that have escalated significantly in recent years:

The Baltic Sea has become "ground zero" for undersea cable targeting. Since 2022, approximately 10 cables have been severed in this region alone, including seven incidents between November 2024 and January 2025. The tactics include:

\- **Anchor dragging** : Ships deliberately dragging anchors to snag cables and pipelines
\- **Suspicious vessel activity** : Russia- and China-linked ships operating under opaque ownership structures near cable routes
\- **Direct attacks** : The Nord Stream pipelines were sabotaged in September 2022, and other energy pipelines connecting Estonia-Finland have been damaged
Multiple nations are implicated in cable threats:

\- **Russia** : Repeatedly named as a possible offender based on ship movements and anchor trails in the Baltic
\- **China** : Increasing activity around Taiwanese cables--five separate cable damage incidents occurred near Taiwan in 2024-2025
\- **Iran** : Iranian state-linked media has explicitly warned of potential attacks on undersea cables in the Persian Gulf, signaling a shift from targeting oil infrastructure to "the invisible" digital backbone
These cables support approximately $9 trillion worth of trade daily. Key strategic concerns include:

1\. **The "Shadow Fleet"**: Aging, poorly maintained tankers and cargo ships operating under flags of convenience that can damage infrastructure while maintaining plausible deniability

2\. **Limited repair capacity** : There are very few dedicated cable repair ships globally. For example, when five of Vietnam's undersea cables were damaged simultaneously in February 2023, repairs took until November 2023 to complete due to vessel shortages

3\. **Choke points** : Critical bottlenecks like the Red Sea, Strait of Malacca, and Mediterranean are vulnerable to concentrated attacks
While accidents cause most day-to-day interruptions, deliberate attacks are growing harder to attribute and prevent. In deeper waters, sabotage requires sophisticated submarines or specialized equipment, but in shallow coastal areas (where many cables lie), simple anchor dragging can cause massive disruption with minimal sophistication.

When cables are cut, nations lose significant data transmission capacity. Vietnam lost 75% of its data capacity during the 2023 cable outages. A coordinated multi-cable attack could isolate entire regions from the global internet.

The threat is so serious that the U.S. established the [Cable Security Fleet](https://substack.com/redirect/61273021-0b32-4e2f-903e-bdb181e84169?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2020 with dedicated cable repair ships, and NATO has increased naval patrols in the Baltic Sea specifically to protect this infrastructure.

Turns out the biggest threat to AI infrastructure might be missiles abroad... and neighbors at home. | | | May 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- In early 2026, the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps launched a series of unprecedented strikes against American data centers in the Middle East, targeting Amazon Web Services facilities in Bahrain and an Oracle data center in Dubai. Iran justified these attacks by claiming that these facilities hosted AI systems used by the U.S. military for intelligence analysis and war simulations. For the first time, hyperscale cloud infrastructure--previously considered civilian technology--had become explicit military targets in a regional conflict. These attacks mark a dangerous evolution in warfare. Data centers, the backbone of the digital economy, are increasingly being recognized as dual-use infrastructure with strategic military value. As the U.S. and its Middle Eastern partners rush to build AI capabilities, they have inadvertently created high-value targets within missile range of adversarial states. The vulnerability of these facilities demonstrates how the physical infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence has become inextricably linked to national security. Yet as policymakers grapple with these geopolitical threats abroad, an equally complex challenge is emerging at home. Across America, local communities are mounting their own resistance against data center expansion--not with missiles, but with zoning laws, protests, and regulatory opposition. The irony is striking; while Iran attacks data centers for being too close to military operations, American communities are fighting them for being too close to homes, schools, and environmental resources. | | ---|---|--- The primary battleground is water. Large AI data centers can consume up to five million gallons of water daily--the equivalent of a small town--to cool the massive server farms that power artificial intelligence. In water-stressed regions from Arizona to Arkansas, residents are increasingly asking why scarce local resources should be diverted to quench the thirst of tech giants. In Little Rock, protesters recently rallied against a proposed Google facility, citing concerns that data center water consumption would drain local lakes and wetlands over the long term. Noise pollution compounds the tension. Cooling systems and server fans generate constant industrial hums that disrupt wildlife, alter animal behaviors, and disturb human sleep patterns. In Chandler, Arizona, the city council unanimously rejected a proposed AI data center in late 2025 due largely to noise concerns raised by nearby residents. Perhaps most ironically, some communities are now opposing data centers precisely because of the military targeting risks revealed by Iran's attacks. Facilities located near military bases--previously seen as secure locations--are now viewed by some residents as potential magnets for foreign strikes or sabotage operations. National security assets have become neighborhood liabilities. The convergence of these pressures creates a precarious moment for American AI infrastructure. The nation is simultaneously racing to expand data center capacity to compete globally while facing opposition from the very communities expected to host them. As Iran demonstrated, data centers are no longer invisible pieces of internet infrastructure; they are contested sites of geopolitical and environmental conflict. Whether they can survive foreign missiles abroad and local opposition at home remains an open question--and one that will shape the future of artificial intelligence development. Data Center Footprint : \- Average data center: Around 100,000-150,000 square feet (about 2-3 acres) \- Hyperscale data centers: About 435,000 square feet (10 acres) or larger \- Latest trend (2025): New AI-focused data centers average about 613,000 square feet--nearly 14 acres per facility \- The buildings themselves are typically massive warehouse-style structures, 2-3 stories high, packed with server racks Military Base Footprint : \- White Sands Missile Range (NM): The largest U.S. military installation at approximately 3.2 million acres (~139 billion square feet) \- Joint Base Lewis-McChord (WA): 414,000 acres (~18 billion square feet) \- Fort Bliss (TX): ~1.1 million acres (~48 billion square feet) \- Fort Hood (TX): ~214,968 acres (~9.4 billion square feet) \- Even "smaller" major bases like Fort Bragg are 160,000+ acres (~7 billion square feet) A single typical Army division installation covers roughly 15,000-40,000 acres--equivalent to about 150-400 average data centers just in land area. To put it another way: The largest military bases are tens of thousands of times larger than data centers. You could fit the entire data center campus for a major tech company inside many military bases and still have room for live-fire training ranges, airstrips, and maneuver areas. This massive difference explains why data centers often seek locations near military bases for perceived security advantages, while occupying a fraction of the physical footprint. Undersea internet cables face multiple serious threats that have escalated significantly in recent years: The Baltic Sea has become "ground zero" for undersea cable targeting. Since 2022, approximately 10 cables have been severed in this region alone, including seven incidents between November 2024 and January 2025. The tactics include: \- Anchor dragging : Ships deliberately dragging anchors to snag cables and pipelines \- Suspicious vessel activity : Russia- and China-linked ships operating under opaque ownership structures near cable routes \- Direct attacks : The Nord Stream pipelines were sabotaged in September 2022, and other energy pipelines connecting Estonia-Finland have been damaged Multiple nations are implicated in cable threats: \- Russia : Repeatedly named as a possible offender based on ship movements and anchor trails in the Baltic \- China : Increasing activity around Taiwanese cables--five separate cable damage incidents occurred near Taiwan in 2024-2025 \- Iran : Iranian state-linked media has explicitly warned of potential attacks on undersea cables in the Persian Gulf, signaling a shift from targeting oil infrastructure to "the invisible" digital backbone These cables support approximately $9 trillion worth of trade daily. Key strategic concerns include: 1\. The "Shadow Fleet": Aging, poorly maintained tankers and cargo ships operating under flags of convenience that can damage infrastructure while maintaining plausible deniability 2\. Limited repair capacity : There are very few dedicated cable repair ships globally. For example, when five of Vietnam's undersea cables were damaged simultaneously in February 2023, repairs took until November 2023 to complete due to vessel shortages 3\. Choke points : Critical bottlenecks like the Red Sea, Strait of Malacca, and Mediterranean are vulnerable to concentrated attacks While accidents cause most day-to-day interruptions, deliberate attacks are growing harder to attribute and prevent. In deeper waters, sabotage requires sophisticated submarines or specialized equipment, but in shallow coastal areas (where many cables lie), simple anchor dragging can cause massive disruption with minimal sophistication. When cables are cut, nations lose significant data transmission capacity. Vietnam lost 75% of its data capacity during the 2023 cable outages. A coordinated multi-cable attack could isolate entire regions from the global internet. The threat is so serious that the U.S. established the in 2020 with dedicated cable repair ships, and NATO has increased naval patrols in the Baltic Sea specifically to protect this infrastructure. 💌 Join our “Letters for our Neighbors” Community Call on 5/19 | | | Hey Peter, Have you seen these gas prices? Healthcare becoming less and less accessible to our communities? Our friends and co-workers losing their jobs to DACA renewal delays? With so much going on at once, we often feel like there’s nothing we can do about it. **That’s because the system is rigged to protect billionaire interests: their power, their wealth, their gain. Not ours.** All across the country, from DACA recipients to U.S. citizens, millions of working people have been forced by our government into a state of survival. All of it is connected: administrative DACA delays that put our neighbors at risk of losing their jobs, war abroad that makes corporations richer, and horror against immigrants here at home. Our friends and co-workers losing their jobs to DACA renewal delays? With so much going on at once, we often feel like there’s nothing we can do about it. body:
Lessons from the Bay View Massacre
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260505-2784)
Peter,
On this day in 1886, about 1,500 workers, most of them Polish immigrants from Milwaukee's South Side, marched on the Bay View rolling mill. They were striking for the eight-hour workday. Governor Jeremiah Rusk had ordered the state militia to fire if the marchers advanced, and seven people were killed, including a child.
No one was ever charged. Rusk's defiant line — "I seen my duty and I done it" — won him a third term and, three years later, a seat in President Harrison's cabinet as the first U.S. Secretary of Agriculture.
The strike was broken, but the movement wasn't. Workers kept organizing, and over the following decades they won the eight-hour day, the weekend, child labor laws, Social Security, and Medicare. None of those things existed in 1886. All of them were won by working people who refused to stop organizing – even in the face of death.
A hundred and forty years later, the fights continue in Wisconsin and across the country, as workers organize against an economy rigged against them.
Amazon warehouse workers are pushing back against punishing quotas. Nurses are striking over unsafe staffing ratios. Teachers are demanding the state finally fund public schools and restore the collective bargaining rights stripped from them by Act 10. Graduate workers and baristas are unionizing for the first time in their industries.
That's what our campaign means when we say “we make better possible:” standing up for what's right, fighting for what's fair, and refusing to be silenced by the people who would rather we kept our heads down.

In solidarity,
Fran
